[h1] Overall about the game [/h1]
[b] So, the game is massive, huge amount of units and all sorts of different tech from different time periods ( even without dlcs ), beautiful graphics, massive maps, nice campaigns with some intresting missions not only go take point and kill (if we are not talking about skirmishes). Controls feels a bit not new player friendly, but after some time everything will be understandable. Another minus is that every mission takes hours to complete, especially skirmishes. If you are into achievments, yeah, here you will spend a lot of time, and money, since to get all the achievments you must have all the dlcs.
[/b]
[h1] Main game [/h1]
[b] A regular game, without DLC, includes Soviet and German companies including skirmishes, here the Soviet missions are the most interesting, as for me, they have no equal here, the German missions are a little less interesting but still very worthy! As for contractions, if you are in the mood for standing for many hours and gradually reaching points, then this is just for you! True, these two nations have enormous advantages in the form of tanks. From the very first battle, the Soviets have excellent tanks that are superior to the German ones, which greatly simplifies the passage, both in the first and in all subsequent skirmishes, but in later periods, the Germans will have tigers, which will be a dangerous enemy. As for the German skirmishes, naturally, they didn’t have tigers from the start, so it will be more difficult to fight T34s and KVs, in which case it will be convenient to capture a couple of such tanks. From the second battle there will be more serious tanks, and this will make the passage much easier.[/b]

[h1] Scorched Earth DLC [/h1]
[b]This DLC adds 8 new missions and new doctrines to multiplayer, unfortunately new doctrines cannot be used in skirmishes, it would be nice to make a big boom! The missions themselves, as far as I remember, were pretty good, especially when they give you a really big gun![/b]

[h1] Talvisota DLC [/h1]
[b]This is an addition showing the events of the winter war (and more), in which Finland comes into the game! Adds company and skirmishes. The company is interesting, it gives you the opportunity to play as super snipers and encourages you to use unusual tactics. The skirmishes here may seem difficult, especially when you don't have the advantage of tanks, and when your enemy certenly does, but in this case most of the work will be done by anti-tank guns and infantry, and anti-tank guns in this game are very powerful! Pro tip - use Irregular doctrine, for me it was the best. [/b]

[h1] Liberation DLC [/h1]
[b]This DLC adds USA, company and skirmishes to the game. The company was pretty cool, they let you try out a lot of modifications of Shermans, and the US itself has cool units. If we talk about skirmishes, then in this case the United States, as for me, is completely inferior in tanks. It is very difficult to use Shermans when there are panthers and tigers against you, Shermans are, firstly, cardboard, and secondly, they simply cannot penetrate panthers and tigers. So, for me, using tanks is not an option. anti-tank guns are very good choice for this, though! [/b]

[h1] Airborne DLC [/h1]
[b]This DLC adds only story company for the US airborne divisions, a total of 12 missions, where for the first time, the developers also added interesting references and achievements for completing secret missions, some achievements are not so easy to get, I personally had to dive into the guides. Also, an excellent innovation is that finally company map has crates with different stuff, as I remember all the crates that are scattered around the map, during the companies of other nations were always empty. However, the downside is that there are no innovations in other game modes or online mode. I personally recommend purchasing, especially if you are a fan of the plot.
[/b]

[h1] About multiplayer [/h1]
[b] Here everything is more complicated, you play not against a bot, which is often strengthened, but against a player. There are domination mode, where you need to inflict more damage on opponents (you can capture points, but the main thing is to inflict more damage, if you captured more points, but inflicted less damage, you lose), there is a battle zone mode (here you need to hold points, I often played 3v3 or 4v4, in this case there are 9 points on the map, which are distributed quite evenly, three points in the center for which you have to fight). There is also the last stand mode, which is also often played, but it is simply necessary to defend points from bots, in general, it is worth trying to pass once. There is also a front line, there are defending side and an attacking side, there is a very strong imbalance in it, the map is very often an open field where you need to capture all the points. Defenders always put mines in this field, and if you play in the late or middle period and if the defenders are Germans, then there may be panthers and tigers there, to which you simply cannot do anything, of course there is always some IS or IS-2, but basically there is almost always not enough time and the defense wins. And there is also a conquest mode, but I have not tried it, i have seen, that the map gradually opens up there. Usually, if there are many players, it is customary to spread out across the map, if you leave some part open, miners can crawl in (yes, miners literally crawled in once and mined the roads in our rear). Here they also really don't like people whose game lags, because if one player freezes, then everyone freezes at once, but this can also be blamed on the very weak optimization of the game. In general, it always feels like the Germans are stronger due to their wunderwaffe, but it is possible to win, in a few games you will get used to it and will already be at the top of the list.
[/b]

This really hurts, but I just can't put up with it anymore. Don't get me wrong - you can have a lot of fun with this game and it's awesome in some regards. But as it stands now, I can't recommend it. I was hoping that this game would've evolved and fixed a lot of the old issues (from MoWAS 2 for example).
Here are some of those issues:

- Pathfinding is (still) atrocious. Sometimes it doesn't work at all. You are better off driving the vehicles yourself. I've had squads be killed because their support takes too long doing slow turns on the way. Sure it's nice to have vehicles follow roads, but sometimes you just want them to go directly to an area. To be fair you can actually give them waypoints, but they will still suffer pathfinding issues.

- AI is (still) incompetent. They won't do much of anything without you. Soldiers get killed because they won’t return fire on that one enemy soldier shooting at them.

- You need to micromanage, which I generally don't mind, but this game takes it to a new level. You sometimes have to order individual soldiers to fire at targets. A whole squad (which costs a lot of resources) can be wiped out by 3-4 enemy soldiers. Even if they are standing right next to them. If you focus on your units on one part of the map, any units that are on another part will be completely destroyed by enemy units.

- What happens if a unit runs out of ammo, will the game tell you? Nope. Will the AI soldiers scavenge weapons and ammo? Nope. You have to look for a small flashing icon above the soldier's heads. Also, vehicles/guns that completely run out of ammo will just sit there and be killed. No reaction to enemy fire (such as dismounting, reversing, etc.)

- Supply trucks are virtually useless. They are great to begin with, but because of the painfully slow time it takes them to refill makes them a waste of resources. And you'll need a lot of them if you want to keep your units fighting.

- Cover and concealment doesn't mean anything. You'd think that a squad in a trench vs. a squad in the open would, most of the time, win. But not in this game. Your infantry squads, even in cover, will be completely wiped by the enemy. Also, soldiers that are in cover will not react to an enemy standing right next to them. Have fun with that.

- Machineguns outrange tank cannons.

- AI units don't target prioritize. A tank can be firing at enemy infantry even if there's an enemy AT-gun firing at it.

- Tanks will turn their turret towards enemy units even if they are far outside the range of its weapons. This means that your hard earned tank might be destroyed by an enemy tank from another direction. You simply cannot force the tank to face its turret where you want it to.

- Some units will flat out refuse your orders. Want that artillery gun to fire at a spot on the map? Sometimes it will just refuse your order and fire at something else.

- There's a move order and an attack order. The attack order is described as having the unit "fight its way" towards the enemy. That's not how it works, units will charge straight into enemy units and kill themselves. This actually worked as it should in earlier games.

- Remember how units that plant satchel charges would run away from them once placed? Not anymore!

- Direct (FPS) control of units is a really awesome feature. It's sad that you seldom get the chance to use it because you have to micromanage all the time. Most weapons are also way to inaccurate.

- Enemy AI units drop smoke grenades when taking fire. But your own units will not unless you specifically tell them to (i.e. go into a menu and click a button).

- Medics will not automatically heal units. Trying to find the specific location to click on a downed soldier is needlessly hard.

- Sometimes your guns (AT, mortars, etc.) will get themselves killed on terrain before reaching the destination you've ordered them to.

- Units repairing damaged vehicles will sometimes just stop doing it (even if they are not under threat). You have to order them several times. This also happens even if there are repair kits available.

- Soldiers digging foxholes will not always go into them once finished.

So that's what I can recall off the cuff. Hopefully many of these issues will be resolved in the future, but I won’t hold my breath. I will return to the game once in a while to scratch that itch, but will leave it again because of the infuriating issues. I'm truly saddened by this. I was hoping for a better game. I will of course amend this review once issues are fixed.

It's amazing they've designed a game that gets less fun the more you play. I unironically believe Soldiers: Heroes of World War 2, the original, original "Men of War", is more of a game than Gates of Hell: Ostfront will ever be. A game with zero quality of life features, the worst tank combat in the entire genre, AI that's dumb as rocks, and where soldiers shout "bullets fear the brave!", is better than GoH ever will ever be.

Why? SHoWW2 is an actual game, designed with intent and desire to be an action WW2 tactics game with simulationist elements. Systems and mechanics were specifically developed in mind to achieve this unique blend of game: inventories, ammo management, simulated cover, direct control.

GoH is an art project expressed using a game engine, with gameplay thrown in because they remembered they were making a game. The developers have done just above nothing to develop or redevelop mechanics to fit the vision of a more traditional, large-scale RTS game. It did not matter in SHoWW2 you had to find cover for all your troops, because you only had three max. Now you have dozens, and they're all too stupid to save themselves from dying or fathom to move a few spaces to have a clear shooting angle. It's not aided in that the AI seems even worse compared to earlier entries. Cannons and tanks seem to be fine with shooting at tanks that cannot be penetrated, AT riflemen love to waste their shots at random infantry, and as most weapons shoot at a range of over a hundred meters, your troops will waste all their ammo at things they'll hardly hit and then cry they're out of ammo.

Like other recent entries in Men of War style games, GoH has a focus on multiplayer rather than singleplayer. In contrast however, the campaign is expansive, at the cost of quality. Many missions are not about testing your skills or putting you in an engaging situation to squirm out of. Instead most missions are defence missions or mind numbing "attack" missions (defence missions in disguise), and being poorly scripted. You'll sit back, do whatever the game tells you to do, watch things explode for about an hour, and that's called a mission. Attacking is generally no better, as the AI is generally passive and will wait patiently for you to steamroll them (and often times switching to being a defend mission).

In one mission, you must set up defences to resist an attack. You're given two engineers, very valuable units as they're the only ones able to create large trenches for your troops. However, there's an event that will take away a random soldier from your troop temporarily to "scout" for the enemy, and your engineers aren't exempt. If you're unlucky, you must restart the entire mission again, as reloading a save won't change who gets selected. If that wasn't enough, you're forced to retreat and aid some allies in a new defensive zone. However, some units arent properly marked to transfer to the zone, resulting in some units being unselectable.

Another time is when you're holding an established line. No matter how well you do, the game will forcefully reveal your secret, powerful AT gun to the enemy, which then immediately gets bombarded by artillery. Additionally, you're also forced to retreat. Not manually, but via an event that piles all your units together to march towards the next zone. Also, they don't forget their orders, so they'll run back to the enemy. Hope you enjoy seeing your troops dying avoidable deaths twice.

I don't play multiplayer, so the closest you're getting is AI skirmish battles. They're not really fun, as obviously the AI can micro an infinite amount of units at once while your soldiers will find some way to trip over a rock when you look away for a second. The game itself is rather fast-paced, yet also having nothing happen at all. It often becomes a stalemate until the AI decides to run into your MG's, which is nice as it keeps the pace up unlike regular soldier AI, which is too cautious and bunches up near walls a lot.

There's also a gamemode called Frontline, where one side defends and the other attacks. It's balance is awful as it favours the attacker. Once the defender is dislodged, you can expect the attacker to snowball with no way for the defender to recover. It does not help most of the maps are terrible for defending.

Why do I have so many hours? Other than I hate myself, a praise I can give GoH is that it's, quite possibility, one of the largest collections of highly detailed models of World War 2 uniforms, weapons, and other military hardware. If you need to know a bizarely specific physical detail no sane person would document for whatever reason, you can use GoH as a way to find it. This also includes more obscure or lesser used hardware during the early war. However, the inventories and composition of units is unreliable, due to game balance or some unknown factor.

To put it precisely: if you want a video game to have fun with (and you don't have any friends), save your money to buy anything else. If you want a source of WW2 hardware to observe in great detail and in full 3D, buy GoH at a discount.

142709113.review:
This has quickly become one of my favorite RTS games. 

[b]+Positives+[/b]
For those who played Company of Heroes 1, older Blitzkrieg games and Men of War, this is an obvious choice.
Difficulty setting ranges from relaxing and easy to excitingly unforgiving.
The game offers wide variety of gameplay and unit options with each army, even customization of units down to each individual soldier and his weapon and helmet which carries over between the Conquest missions so that everything you've captured or picked up, loaded into truck or else, stays with you until you lose it in combat somehow.
A nifty feature this game has is direct unit control. It lets you to take manual control of a single soldier or vehicle in both top down and third person view, allowing you to make a real difference on the ground yourself, if the situation demands it.
I am not much of a linear campaign player, but the game offers sprawly sets of linear missions for each nation. 
Dynamic campaign is a wonderful offense-defense based set of randomized missions in between which you prepare your unit composition. It feels more like each battle is a fresh skirmish, but with your veteran army you have built along the way.
Then of course, battles and skirmishes for both singleplayer and multiplayer.

[b]-Negatives-[/b]
Controls might feel a little clumsy and not immediately responsive, especially in third person direct control mode. This comes in the form of unpleasant "freezes" of your character or vehicle mid-animation, preventing any action for a brief moment. It is consistent enough, so you can likely get used to it.
Fog of war is slightly misleading, even though it feels like the more interesting way to play the game. Units tend to ignore it at times, shooting accurately without direct line of sight. This applies to both, your units and enemies. At times your men will shoot at enemy that you can not even see indicated on the map or in the field. 
There are still a few bugs, but all in all the fun this game offers easily outweights them.

142690159.review:
This is on of the best RTS I've ever played. Amount of content is insane, I have 100+ hours on record and barely scratched the surface, mostly because I've been hooked up on dynamic campaign mode. But regular campaign missions are as good: they're diverse, they provide a challenge and many of them allow very different approaches adding to replayability. They also provide some of very unique scenarios that are underrepresented in WWII games like defending against the Red Army under Leningrad as spanish Blue Division or acting as a rear guard for the Red Army units retreating from Kerch peninsula, not to mention the whole Finland campaign.

Excessive attention to details like the full damage model for each vehicle including static weapons or ability to control individual units and tampering with their inventory provides a handful of tactical possibilities and greately contributes to the uniqueness of battles making each one a story in its own right. It also looks very cinematic and you truly feel like you're watching some good WWII movie with that amount of chaos and unexpected situations.

It's worth its money even when there's no sale. You'll also appreciate the friendliness to modding, absence of money-grabbing in form of in-game stores or microtransactions. It has DLC's, yes, but each one contributes to the game greately, adding a lot of new units, maps and singleplayer campaign missions.

10/10

Review of singleplayer: 

Price/Style of gameplay:

not for the price... hell no. The game is a moderate copy of assault squad 2 with better graphics. There's a 3rd person direct control mode, which is the only new thing compared to assault squad 2 in terms of new features. 

The missions seem kind of boring with the, here's 2 tanks, now go destroy the whole enemy army of 10000 men, style of gameplay.. 

I never liked that type of gameplay, from the previous men of war titles.

I always preferred playing big battles with the ability of a lot of reinforcements, so far I haven't ecnountered that in Gates of Hell.

AI:

The AI is crap, just like in every other comparable men of war style game.

Here's an example, the medics don't revive fallen soldiers, you have to micro-manage that... come on...  The units don't use cover properly, resulting in them all dying very fast to the enemy which makes the whole thing of limited amount of units for 1 battle completely useless. I need a lot of infantry that act as cannon fodder to go through trenches. You cannot rely on them doing the job properly on their own they don't know how to effectively use cover, they stroll around mindlessly and die to an enemy mg emplacement because instead of jumping for cover they act as if the mg wasn't even firing at them.. this lack of smart behavior just demonstrates how crazy outdated the AI of the engine is. 

Here's another example, while I'm playing the mission siege of Sevastopol. There are a huge amount of trenches and I'm only given a limited amount of units. My infantry gets depleted fast and dies. I'm given a small assortment consisting of 1x Stug, 1x panzer 3 and 1x panzer 4 along with 1x large artillery mortar, to destroy around 1000 enemy infantry, who are all well entrenched and have defensve positions with AT gun emplacements, mg nests etc. This battle could have been made so much more fun by just introducing reinforcements, more tank types, maybe fighter planes as support...

I could understand how for some people it might seem as a fun challenge, but to me it just feels boring, with me having to go into 3rd person in a singular tank and kill entrenched infantry 1 by 1 manually ESPECIALLY IF THE WHOLE BATTLE EVOLVES TO BE JUST THAT because you can forget sending units out on their own and expecting any positive results.

I wish the battle was more self-sustainable, as in, where you just right click and send units in a direction and they're able to actually utilize cover do advances on their own, move in smart patterns, medics who heal units, units who pick up ammo from a dead soldier next to them in order for them to resupply when they run out of ammo, ALL OF THIS without me having to 
 MANUALLY babysit them.. Then I could imagine that the 3rd person direct control would actually make sense because then I could actually feel immersed in the battle without having to worry about nonsense like resupplying a single soldier when I have like a 100 other soldiers that require the same attention...

The AI should be capable to do more on its own, come on it's 2023, not 2010...

Crashes / Problems:

The game crashes every now and then when I try to reload a saved game. 
I've also noticed while in 3rd person, if I'm in a trench the enemy has aimbot like precision and instantly kills. The collision inside a trench when clearing it is also weird. Imagine I'm in an L shaped trench, with the enemy on one end and me being on the other end inside 3rd person direct control. The enemy can with pinpoint precision shoot and kill me while they are prone.. through 10 meters of thick earth and mud...this just ruins the immersion, come on guys, this should've been done better... 

The camera is focused in a way so that when you're in 3rd person, you're viewing your soldier on the left side of your screen, there's no way to change that perspective, so that the soldier is on the right hand side of your screen, which caused me to die a bunch of times because I was forced to go around the whole trench, to shoot the enemy who was hiding. That's just ridiculous, camera controls aren't that hard to implement, something this simple should be in the game. 

The game also automatically assumes that I have a mouse with extra buttons which not everyone does. There should be a configuration for people who don't have extra buttons on their mouse but rather want to use their keyboard. Example is let's say, to make it easier to switch to a grenade while in 3rd person or a hotkey to switch grenade types or switch to a pistol from a rifle... in order to do any of those things I had to manually exit 3rd person and hover over the thing with the mouse... there should be hotkeys on the keyboard for this.

One more thing I noticed while using the 3rd person mode. The enemy AI shoots through obstacles. There is absolutely no regard to line of sight. They shoot you through a thick forest. This is just plain bad... How am I supposed to be immersed if the enemy shoots me with aimbot like precision through thick forests? What is even the point in 3rd person direct control then?

Overall:

It's a mess.. a lot of things could've been done better and should be improved for the price tag that they're asking for the DLCs and the game itself. All I can see as of right now is an overly glorified graphics mod for the original base game from 2009 men of war, with maybe slightly updated AI but it's not any better than, if for comparison, you gave a caveman a rifle and pointed him towards a ww2 battlefield.. the behavior of the AI is somewhat similar to that.

If you've read this, I sincerely hope that you, DO NOT think, I'm being harsh with this review. This game is not a standalone game. It requires you to purchase the base game Call to Arms itself in order to play it. It will cost 45 euros WITHOUT any additional DLCs. You want the DLCs for this "DLC game", add another 25 euros on top of that.... this is such an enormous price tag!!!!!!! FOR a game that is less than optimal, considering it's release in 2021 and 2023 standards and expectations. All the problems I mentioned above are legitimate and their existence is unjustified.

This is an amazing rts! I've never gotten into any WW2 rts games before the Men of War games or even since then, so this (the Men of War franchise and Gates of Hell) is my first foray. In particular in the new dynamic campaign mode. And there's never a moment where I feel like the game is dull. I'm always engaged and at the edge of my seat, as even the best laid plans can quickly go awry if I'm not careful. 

The only things I would have to say as negatives against this game are that multiplayer "versus" matches cannot be saved, especially for when making longer games; and that the dynamic campaign isn't set up for player vs player, but rather is only co-op. Players also still cannot enter into savable co-op where you can play through the long singleplayer missions together (couldn't save in Men of War: Assault Squad 2 co-op missions, either, which really hurt that experience due to how long and grueling some of those missions were, much like some of these). However, dynamic campaign mode is savable for those great, long team-ups. 

But, if it's possible at all to make it so in the coding of this game, having a pvp style dynamic campaign is a must. It disappoints me greatly that this isn't in the game given how incredible this mode is. It seems like a perfect mode tailor made for pvp. So I hope this gets implemented as soon as possible--assuming it's even possible to do so. Even if only 1v1.

One of the very best WW2 strategy games I've ever played. It's a bit rough around the edges in places, but is engaging and immersive like no other game in the genre. Don't be scared off by the tutorial - it is not very representative of the overall experience, and the game overall is a lot more strategic and less focused on micromanagement than the tutorial would suggest.

In many ways, comparing Ostfront to say, Company of Heroes, is quite alike comparing Battlefield to Call of Duty - both are great games, but take very different approaches in style and scale. Ostfront is far more of a simulation and goes to huge lengths to have its locations feel like real places, its units behave how you would in real life, and the moment-to-moment considerations feel more grounded in the setting than as a layer of abstraction. Thanks to its grand scale, ability to take direct control of units, and atmospheric presentation, you really feel like commanding over a real battle in a way that is rare for these kind of games.

Overall, Ostfront is a fantastic experience for anyone who enjoys deep, complex and engaging strategy games in a WW2 setting. It is extremely replayable and a huge amount of fun, only held back by its lack of polish in places and its vague presentation of how everything works. Both these are things that do keep improving and likely only will more so over time.

A very strong recommendation!

Greatest WW2 RTS ever so far. Many improvements since similar games like MOWAS2, and better than its main concurrect that is Company Of Heroes 3 (meh). The attention to detail, the authenticity, the sounds, the mods, everything is here to make you feel like a child playing with his toy soldiers again. 

Even better, there is an Editor where you can create maps and scenarios for yourself and friends and community. There is only one stain on this feature though, whenever you create a map, it modifies your game files and you can't play online with anyone unless they have this map as well, which is quite annoying and forces you to get the files to your friend or to move the map/scenario files out of your game directory or reinstall the game entirely.

Features are great and the game feels immersive, I get a ton of joy from just watching battles unfold with troops taunting and screaming, yet I crave for more QoL features.

The main feature of the game and what most people are looking for in my humble opinion, is replayability and the conquest mode, which, even though it gets updated once in a while, is underdevelopped and deserves more attention. Also, why can't I get panzergrenadiers in conquest when I can get them in multiplayer ?

The AI is great (maybe too great ?) and will give a challenge to rookie players even on the easiest difficulty.

DLCs are great and not overpriced (Talvisota adds a whole faction, a new campaign, around 40 maps and new units, 15€ on full price but usually on sale (7,50€ at the time of writing this).

I've never had a bug in the vanilla game, however the game won't support too many mods, and the load order is important and can sometimes be hard to get right.

Overall I strongly recommend this game to anyone that's into the WW2 time period and any people looking for a good looking/sounding RTS game.

I look forward to its future (USA faction incoming with unseen battles and new mechanics, La Pointe Du Hoc is one of them) and especially more Quality Of Life ! Please for the sake of all !

141063403.review:
After almost 500 hours of playtime I can say that this game is definitely the king of the RTS genre at the moment. Here are some of the biggest points this game has to its name.

By far the biggest part of this game is micro. You need to focus on a a unit to put them into a good position but are also aware of all other units on the battlefield. This also means that there is always things to do but you can never get them all done, and you may miss big opportunities. This game is really for people who always want to be an active role in the battle and not as much for those who want to lay back and let the units do their thing. This is a pro and a con depending on your own play-style.

The second factor which might lead people towards and away from the game is realism. This is great as you get to experience the closest thing to a ww2 battle from a birds eye view. It also means that your units are not invincible. If you spend a bunch of points on a Tiger or IS-2, it can get taken out in an instant by a large AT-gun or infantry anti-tank weaponry.  There is always a risk for every unit. This will bring a lot of rage to the game but also satisfaction.

mods are important to keep many games fun and saturated. CTA GOH is no different. This does not mean that it is necessary for the game, but you will find that after a while, it gets repetitive.

Many people have noted how the AI is less than perfect... A lot less than perfect. This may cause players to rage as to why the supply trunk is driving in front of your tank or infantry taking the worst possible path. The dev team is trying to fix some of the issues related to AI, but it only means that you need to take a bit more care with your units. A little more management, but it is worth it.

Explosions...Just explosions. I like them. You will probably like them. Combined with destructible entities, it is incredibly satisfying.

The price is very high, way too high for what it is. but during steam sales, it drops by 75%. Take advantage of it!

There are many more points, some bad, lots of good, but in my opinion, it is the best around.

Honestly? The best damn WW2 RTS I've ever played. Enjoying this one immensely and I don't even like RTS games that much in the first place.

It's hugely immersive and you can even control single units in 3rd person action game style. The attention to detail is one of the best I've seen in the genre and it's super fun with buddies online. 

The sounds are fantastic too. Even the units sound really good and they shout out useful things such as warning you about tanks, machine guns, when they need a medic or more ammo instead of just generic unit action blabber such as "Alright!" and "Copy!" provided you can understand the language that is.

The game is very micro heavy though. There are so many little things you can and often must do while you command the units, such as inventory management, first aid, reloading guns and keeping the gears of war well oiled. This is a non issue however as the game is more about intelligent troop positioning and pressing the advantage when it benefits you the most. A small handful of well positioned soldiers can deal a lot of damage to the enemy.

It can all get a little overwhelming occasionally and you'll likely get your ass handed back, but I find that losing is also quite fun. Something I rarely experience in regular RTS games, the few I've played. They just don't appeal to me at all, but this game for some odd reason does.

The biggest flaw I've noticed is perhaps the AI of your own troops. As I said, the game is pretty micro heavy and you need to babysit them a lot in certain situations and if that situation happens to be one where there is action all over the map, you're going to lose troops just because they can't save themselves.

Other than that it's a great game. Can't recommend it enough.

I have many positive things to say about this game, however I have a LOT of negatives to point out that, quite frankly have started to quite thoroughly tick me off. On top of that have solutions that can fix this. I have experienced ALL of these issues within ONE match.

Before posting, a disclaimer, this is not a "skill issue" it is a fundamental mechanic issue that needs fixing at the base level.

1. Mortars and artillery, attack ground options often do not work despite there being nothing in the way of the order. I have to issue the command anywhere from 3-6 times before my artillery goes "Oh hey, you know what..? Maybe I should actually fire a few shells towards that enemy artillery battery that is killing my mates.. that is a good idea I see your point". Artillery that has hostiles in it's vicinity SHOULD be able to follow their attack ground orders seemlessly, MOWAS did not have this issue, and I cannot see why it persists.
2. Tank autism, yes this is the proper word. Let me pitch this scenario for you: You have a tank, it's dug in for some extra protection, it's left flank up against a building and it's right and forward exposed. And you have another position farther down on the left. Now this position is being attacked by enemies on the right. Does this entrenched position engage? No why would it do that! It has a juicy tank, that it can't fire at through the building, so why on earth would it fire at the exposed enemies? I couldn't imagine why! "Oh but sir... the enemies on the other side of this building, NOWHERE near me are much more pressing than the enemies exposed firing at me right now"
2 A. Another scenario: you order your tank to fire at an exposed crew serve, like an emplaced gun, it's in an open field no cover. Then you go off to issue some more commands to some other troops, look back at this tank and what has it done? "Sir... well quite frankly... I know this crew serve is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up your infantry, but I decided to say ♥♥♥♥ that and engage something else instead. What? Oh no it's actually very easy for me to hit, I just didn't feel like it. What? I was moving at it to shoot when you issued the command? Yeah about that, I thought your orders were stupid so I did something else" And now I lost 3 squads.

Oddly enough, infantry do not have this issue, it appears to be only an issue with armoured vehicles, and my solution to fix the tank crews being literally retarded, is a simple one. Tanks should have an order that gives them sectors of fire, or at the very least priority targets. That way my tank doesn't go full ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and try to fire through a building while actively being shot at.

Vehicles should prioritize automatically, hostiles they can see over someone they cannot, ie.. fix the bloody AI.

I don't know why this problem has persisted throughout the game since it's release, it is beyond me. You would think these issues would have been ironed out by now, unless the devs thought tank crews not having brains would be a grand feature.

RANT OVER
-------------

The game is still to this day one of the best WWII RTS games out there, and I highly recommend it, but my god.. some of the mechanics in this game are beyond frustrating in pitched battles, especially when every second and every order counts. Also I have brought this up in Q&As and the dev responses have been: "We don't see this as a severe enough issue". Understandable.
Great game, but devs that give the "Good enough" pass on mechanics is just not the greatest thing in the world

UPDATE: While some problems still persist, I'd say the devs have addressed a lot of the prior issues. Their mission design is still just... awful. It's common to get sniped by new enemies as you're cutscene-transitioned to new parts of it.

But Skirmish? It's great, especially with mods as they are now. Thanks to that, I know I'm going to keep loving playing this with friends for awhile to come

... so long as AI doesn't break again.

UPDATE: Mission design is just terrible. Compared to their work in Men of War, missions frequently give you vague objective descriptions. This means that you'll be preparing a defense for objectives without an understanding of where the enemy is actually coming from. You spend 15+ minutes setting up minefields and machine gun positions, only for the missions to go "Ha! Idiot! You should've guessed that the enemy would've been tank rushing from the South." It basically demands you either get some info on the forums or replay just to have a chance at enjoyably playing some of these missions.

Update mission descriptions and make the invasion attack arrows appear during defense setup stages.

EDIT: Infantry AI is unbelievably broken right now. They will forget to follow your commands or take a long time to comply. They'll barely shoot back and only seemingly under very specific circumstances. It's as if they're all stuck to Return Fire behaviour, more or less. This means you end up babying your frontlines a lot more, and coming back to other parts to find it blown to smithereens as you lost the initial trade of volleys. 

This is currently nigh-on non-functional and takes a great deal of the fun out of the game. Furthermore, click-dragging infantry squads into cover produces odd results that often just get them kill. 

Advancing requires constant Direct Control usage in order to have a hope in hell of hitting entrenched positions before they annihilate your helpless little ducklings. 

Finally, firefights have become deadly accurate. You barely need anyone to have snipers, as the first bullet out of an MG can sometimes laser through the enemy infantries heads with comical precision. We once had an enemy medic come around a corner and dome three of our men in the heads before any of them got a shot off. Funny, but too common.

The game in this state threatens to sour it for me and my friend, who have loved this game throughout all it's iterations, even given it's jankiness then.

P.S: Make ammo trucks replenish the equipped weapon, not the one they spawned with. It's just less fun. I don't care about immersion and realism here. It's already enough of a slog sometimes without this.

138618880.review:
Probably one of my favourite games of all time. It was a little rough after launch with performance, ai issues and bugs, but most problems have been handled and the game is pretty smooth except for a few janky moments when interactions like sandbags, repairing, grenades and that get interrupted or happen on jagged terrain.

This game is by far the best ww2 rts game, its realistic but not too realistic that your tanks can't see anything and get shot from 3km away. Infantry health is just right (and if not for you just get one of the many mods) where good infantry feel incredibly useful and direct controlling makes you feel like a hero of the soviet union, but not a superhero.

Tank combat is incredibly well done, the focus on early barb makes for interesting tank fights that are forgotten in other ww2 games where it usually just pz4, panther and tiger vs t34/85 and IS2. You always have a tool up your belt to deal with big threats, whether its a crazy blitz trying to rear pen the KV1, calling in bombs on IS2s, using your arty direct fire or charging hordes of infantry just to get one satchel thrown.

The campaign missions are pretty good, some are better than others, and some needing just a few changes to be great. Only critique I would give is to make a tool that enables building defenses and placing mines on click to speed up the setup phase rather than 30 min of selecting a guy to go pickup mine then set him to place it. The creativity that you come up with when having to deal with large threats when you only have limited AT is very fun. I remember how satisfying it was to verse a column of pz1 and 2s and a bison with only a PTRD and hitting the ammo detonate.

The skirmish modes (ones where you push to take the 7 points and unlock units) can get a little formulaic, but are always good fun, and some of them on hardcore get incredibly hectic like the battle of Berlin.

The faction balance is reasonable, Soviets are pretty strong but have weakpoints that are covered with other units, but Germans have weakpoints but are a little more versatile. For example, German rifle squads with an mg42 beat the early Soviet rifles that only have Mosins and a DP, but once Soviets start getting more SVT and especially PPSh then they dominate the short and mid range, but Germans always do well at long range using the double mg42 squads. In late war the German infantry using Sturmgewehr are incredibly versatile and strong with strong AT, only outmatched by Sturmoviki and Osnaz. Finnish as expected aren't a superpower, but with lots of PzShrecks they can sorta hold out, they use a lot of funky artillery and aa guns that do quite well against weak armour. Strangely though the WW1 Finnish arty has better accuracy and rof than Soviet arty, but i suspect that is intentional to give them something good.

Only some units stand out as a little too good that might need some kind of nerf. All short barrel 150mm weapons IG33, KV2 and that feel a little too good at killing heavy armour, maybe just a little nerf. The Ig15 is ridiculously good with exellent heat, too accurate and fast rof HE and the best possible arc to shoot from behind terrain.

Soviets and Germans have matchups that reflect history; at the start of barb the early KV1 and T34 are incredibly fearsome tanks to try and beat with at best PzIII L and Pz4 F1, it's only when you get the Pak40 do you start to stand a chance. You react and get the Tiger (rushing the tiger or any heavy AT as germans is essential in conquest) and it does well, but still as happened in my game got blown up by KV2, hit with Br-2, katyusha'd and IL2'd. You never feel completely safe, and the strong yet balanced and reasonable accessible artilleries provide an excellent counter to the typical meta in WW2 RTS of just getting the heaviest tank.

Direct controlling is in its best form here, better than all other Men of Wars, on launch it used to be such a big buff that you pretty much had to, to now being just enough to be fun but not necessary to win. It's nice to have total control of a unit and not lose a game to unit ai problems as happens in many rts games. It enables very creative plays and really makes you use all the small stats like turret traverse, turret rotation speed, rear armour, reverse and acceleration, turning circle, even the rear mg on the KV1, no other rts makes those things matter as much.

Most RTS (like Steel Divison) have few maps that get repetitive and kill replayability, the large number of different maps, attack angles and point locations give a lot of variety in attacking distances and defensive style. I hope they keep up the regular addition of maps and even support some of the modders that are adding maps. And please allow some of the great maps in campaign and conquest to be in multiplayer. 

Tavisota should be able to be disabled in conquest, as it was often just kind of annoying fighting finnish, as they aren't much of a threat to a well put together force, just slow to clear out. Tavisota has some fun campaign missions and are an ok addition to conquest, and being only a bit of a meme in multiplayer. Get this if you have already played all the content in the base game.

Scorched earth only adds a few units, but some that should have been in the base game. There needs to be more SPAA to help with anti-infantry, as well as more shredder crew weapons. The flakvierlung dominated MOWAS2 but it should be in the game maybe at a decently high cost or available with doctrine. Only adding the werbelwind leaves soviets with only the T60 as a dedicated anti-infantry light tank. There are some cool things here, just none that change things up and these should have been in the base game.

The devs are doing well, just wish they would handle and improve grenade ai, remove a bit of jank with crewed weapons, make repairing better (I don't want to have to click repair 5 times and have the guy get out and in 5 times before he decides to repair the tread), fix some issues of multiplayer desyncing with some hits not counting and tanks being killed by an ally but still showing as an enemy for you. Improving the offensive ai in conquest is something that is steadily happening, but still the drive the weak tanks down the road to get one shotted each time then charge infantry into 4 mgs is a little unimmersive. Some ui changes that make hotkeys more better (they often get removed if you decided to manually change them) but also able to tell me at a glance ammo level of main gun and who in the squad has which grenade. More bunkers, units, maps, all would be great.

138556828.review:
[h3]My thoughts:[/h3]
[i]Gates of Hell[/i] is the best iteration of the RTS genre to date. Set during World War 2, the game feels like an authentic combat experience. No other RTS has come close to reproducing the excitement, let downs, and random cinematic moments that occur during battle.

[h3]What I like:[/h3]
[*][u][b]Asymmetrical Warfare.[/b][/u] 
There is no rock-paper-scissors balancing here. Your infantry are going to get shredded by MGs and field guns without proper armor support. GOH gets compared to [i]Company of Heroes[/i] a lot but it plays so differently it feels like it might as well be in a separate genre.[*][u][b]Combined Arms.[/b][/u]
That feeling of pushing an objective with infantry, armor, and indirect fire support in a tandem effort is unmatched. 
[*][u][b]Direct control.[/b][/u] 
Being able to take control of the tanks in real time with WASD and using your mouse to aim the turret never gets old. Every station (Commander, Gunner, MG Gunner, etc) is available to use. So if you want to use the radio operators MG while the turret reloads go ahead! You can even have the commander open the hatch to use the cupola MG.
[*][u][b]Inventory system.[/b][/u] 
All units in the game can share items, ammo, and other things which adds to immersion. I love being able to see the physical differences between the cannon ammo types (AP, HE, WP, etc)
[*][u][b]Logistics are acknowledged.[/b][/u] 
I love that you can use trucks to tow artillery, field guns, and auto-cannons around. There are specific trucks for ammo, fuel, and supply to keep your army functioning. You can repair your own equipment as well as steal enemy equipment and repair them too. It's so nice to see that this "unsexy" side of war is addressed.
[*][u][b]Several game modes.[/b][/u] 
Story missions are my favorite with the dynamic campaign a close second, both of which can be played in COOP with 4-8 people. The two skirmish modes are fun as comp stomps as well.
[*][u][b]Tons of maps.[/b][/u] 
Crazy detailed environment. So much work went into filling the maps with detritus and articles of war strewn about. They really feel lived in. Some of the missions are made using aerial reconnaissance from the war. There are probably 100 different maps with all the DLC included.
[*][u][b]Amazing graphics and effects.[/b][/u] 
I still remember the first time I saw  a tank cook off. Then when I realized it wasn't just a canned effect it just blew my mind. There is a penetration system regarding armor in this game. Know where the ammo storage is on a certain tank? If you pen it there you'll get a devastating ammo rack that obliterates the tank
[*][u][b]Immersive sound design.[/b][/u] 
The sound from units and effects like gunshots morph depending on how far the game camera is to the source. There are even separate sound effects when you are in third/first person view. There are different sounds for shell ricochets and penetration which are very satisfying to hear. I particularly like the sound of the Tiger's main cannon.
[/list]
[h3] What I dislike: [/h3] 
[*][u][b]So much jank.[/b][/u] 
Issues with unit pathing, AI, and bugs. The more you play the less it affects you but this is a real problem that turns new players away.
[*][u][b]Performance issues.[/b][/u] 
Even with a 13th Gen i7 and RTX 4080, at 3440x1440 resolution the frame rates can dip into the 60s and lower under certain circumstances. Mostly it plays smoothly. Crashing doesn't happen that often but can be frustrating when it does.[/list] 
[h3] Wishlist: [/h3] 
[*][u][b]Join in progress.[/b][/u] 
It would be really nice to have a drop in and drop out system for friends. Currently you have to start a mission over if a friend disconnects for connectivity reasons. Sometimes you have to decide whether to end a game early or finish the mission while your buddy waits because of this issue.
[*][u][b]Ability to save progress in COOP mode.[/b][/u] 
This would also more or less solve the previous problem.
[*][u][b]Assign units to the player that bought them.[/b][/u] 
Currently in COOP Story missions the game will randomly assign units to all players regardless of who purchased them. This leads to micro-management of giving the units to the player that wanted them in the first place, which disrupts the flow of the other players.
[*][u][b]More Logistics.[/b][/u] 
I would love to see a system where a recovery vehicle could tow tank hulls off the battlefield for repairs in safer locations. An engineer could build a vehicle field repair structure that would serve as faster means to repairs and additionally to resupply of repair kits for vehicles.
[*][u][b]More air support.[/b][/u] 
Currently there are a couple of off-map air call-ins that you can do. I'd love to see some way to include how the air war impacted the battles. Some ability to drop paratroopers would be awesome.
[*][u][b]More theaters of World War 2.[/b][/u] 
I'd love to see North Africa, Pacific, Italy, etc.

An offer you can't refuse: Get ready for the ultimate WW2 tactical simulation.

Although it's not quite a complete masterpiece, it's the closest thing I've found to one for this genre. The developers are dedicated to updating this game and it's exciting to think of the untapped potential waiting to be unleashed.

The gameplay mechanics are gripping! You really feel like you're commanding your digital army to victory, or being pushed back into defeat. You can switch to directly controlling individual units through third person or first person view which, while remaining a somewhat clumsy feature, can be a very satisfying experience and can be used for a tactical edge. There are many units available to you and they follow closely to historical lines. It's up to you to put them to their best use. 

Graphics-wise, it's a real treat for the eyes. The visuals are so stunning, I sometimes wish I had a better computer to truly savor them. 

The user interface and controls are pretty seamless, though there are moments when I wish there were additional ways of actually being in control. A good addition to this game was how you are able to select a squad of perhaps 12 units and spread them out across cover over a large area just by clicking and dragging. These sorts of features are extremely useful and could use more expansion. Something I'd like to see is a control that tells units to "stay-in-cover" so that it's not a constant micromanagement. It can be be frustrating. The game flow can easily get overwhelming, as if I need to be everywhere and controlling everything all at once with limited capabilities.

I appreciated the story missions since they draw you right into the WW2 atmosphere and get your feet wet. There are many missions that I have yet to try out. However, this game really shines with the multiplayer.

One thing I've noticed is the wide skill gap between players. You'll need practice and determination to master the game and stay fierce on the battlefield. The good news? Victory is very satisfying. The experience will keep you hooked for hours on end. I lost count of my multiplayer matches. You can use each one honing your strategic prowess and unveiling new aspects of your personal warfare style.

If you're looking for an engaging WW2 tactical simulation that'll keep you hooked for hours, press the buy button. Trust me, you won't regret it.

136819440.review:
In an age when the WW2 game market is saturated with nonsense games with titles like Hitler's BDSM bunker, making a mockery of the scale and importance of this dramatic human event, then you have games like CTA:GOH that respect their source material, while having enjoyable gameplay. In my opinion this is the best WW2 rts game out right now, and certainly the one most worthy of praise to be released in recent memory. My review will be from the perspective of someone who is casual and does not play competitively. I play strictly against AI opponents, so keep that in mind.

One of my favorite things about this game is the heightened realism when you compare it with other WW2 rts games. This isn't the gimmicky, arcadey gameplay of Company of Heroes or even Steel Division. There is no base-building and are no bullet sponge soldiers here. The combat is more visceral, things feel like they have more 'weight' behind them, and the scenery is nicer to look at. Many parts of the environment can be destroyed and knocked over, such as trees and buildings. The wreckage, death and destruction lend themselves to the feeling that an actual battle took place. I feel like this can still be improved further, though. I would love to see fires lasting longer, and more instances of buildings, debris and soldiers catching on fire, as well as charred remains and so on. This is there to some degree, but I hope they'll build on it further.

The micromanaging aspect of the game may scare some players, but it isn't as bad as you might think. The difficulty parameters can be changed to give you more or less of a challenge, and when you're playing against AI you usually don't need to play optimally anyway. A good idea to get acquainted with the game a bit is to fire up a skirmish match with an AI and yourself against another AI. Your AI ally can keep the enemy busy while you practice, test out equipment, and so on. The AI itself can cheat, as well as do dumb things at times, but it isn't a huge issue, and the developers continue to improve upon them in subsequent updates. As far as mircomanaging, you can control a individual soldier, or group of soldiers at once. You can toggle first person or third person mode while controlling a soldier. Controlling everything at once isn't completely necessary, you can get your guys into strategic positions and start advancing slowly, or you can be more aggressive and micro-heavy. I prefer the more methodical, casual approach. I mention this mainly so people know that you don't have to be super competitive to play the game. Currently the game has the Soviet Union, Germany and (with DLC) Finland as playable nations. The DLCs are recommended, albeit overpriced in my opinion. 

Let me talk about some suggestions for future updates/DLCs that I think would improve the game. Some of this stuff has been implemented to some extent, but could be increased a great deal. A proper dlc focused strictly on Operation Barbarossa. A lot would need to be done to do proper justice to this largest invasion in history. It would need to include Axis soldiers from not only Germany, but their puppets and satellites that took part in the invasion, namely: Finland, Romania, Italy, Croatia, Slovakia, and Hungary. A way of doing this without making all of those countries as separate factions (which obviously would take A LOT of work) would be to give them as auxillary and complementary troops within the greater German roster. The variety of units, the massive amount of troops involved, and the speed and encircling maneuvers could make this very interesting gameplay. The 1939 invasion of Poland is another frontrunner for new content that could be added. These are all just ideas, but I can't wait to see what comes next with this game.

The game already has quite a few mods and there seem to be more noteworthy ones arriving each week. Mods are highly recommended. Not only can they change up aspects of the game that you might find need tweaking, some also change the game completely, such as the Vietnam mod or the Russian Civil War mod. Take a look at the workshop and see what interests you.

And there you go, my jumbled thoughts about Call to Arms - Gates of Hell Ostfront! It's already a great game, one that can be and still does get improved and updated. In an era where most WW2 games are oversaturated, weird, and lackluster I can easily recommend Gates of Hell to those interested in a rts game with a WW2 setting.

This game is yet another (how many do we have now... six?) version of the good old soldiers game, way back from 2004. Instead of making a new and more optimised engine, the devs have decided to make yet another, more polished clone of the same thing. 
The game has its unique way of managing battlefield and way more indepth feel of everything going around (explosions, sound effects, the sheer variety of units and weapons beat any wannabe WW2 game like CoH...). Unfortunately... it's nothing new and while being a lot more enjoyable, the engine always came with its quirks and troubles.

So here's a list of my overall gripes that eventually made me not recommend this game (and probably give up on it until devs decide to fix the underlying issues):

- First up is the abyssmal AI that controls all the units on the battlefield. Units are sometimes endlessly stupid and can't execute the most simple of commands without dying in some stupid way. Direct control is the only redeeming factor (which to dev's credit has been improved)

- Campaigns are okay and they can provide all the enjoyment for a bogstandard single player fans. I wouldn't recommend trying to come close to any of the multiplayer modes though (including any of the co-op modes).

- And this is the main reason why i stopped playing - multiplayer has been totally ruined by making the netcode unstable to the point of being literally unplayable. Units are rubberbanding and teleporting through the ENTIRE MAP. FPS randomly drops every second and is super inconsistent (so you can dream of having any direct control). I feel like i don't have any control over the battlefield because i'm constantly seeing teleporting and glitching units so i don't really see any point in actually trying to play. 

- And for the love of god... The UI in any of the coop modes should be separate for every player... This is something that has been persistent since MoW:AS and is annoying like hell. Having your interface tab change randomly right when you click to call some unit because your ally decided he want to call something else... it is just infuriating.

To sum up, game has great potential but devs prefer to release more and more releases, piling up more errors on top of this huge existing mound of problems, insead of fixing their releases. I'm going to wait until they finally decide to fix their stuff and i recommend that to everyone else.

134492944.review:
After 1276 hours in GoH, I feel it's time to leave an honest and unbiased review. (maybe)

Gates of Hell is a RTS game set in World War 2 released in 2021, it has seen 3 DLC's, 5 Content Updates and 3 Community Updates with many smaller updates so far.

GoH for an RTS is pretty demanding specs. wise. The graphics though pretty to the eye are demanding and performance heavy at times.
The games sound design is second to none, in the RTS genre GoH has probably the best sound design I've ever seen.

Together with the great graphics and sound design are: Vehicle and Infantry models, and they look incredible.
The vehicles (especially the newer ones) come in a stunning amount of detail and historical accuracy, some of the older vehicles have sadly fallen behind graphics wise, they are simply outdated compared to the newer ones.


To go with the amazing models the game features an Amazing damage model for Vehicles. Instead of a plain healthbar, the game models multiple componets of vehicles with various stages of damage:
- Guns can be broken
- Tracks destroyed
- Ammuniton cooked off
- And Additional armor such as skirts and track shot right off

This means tank engaments aren't just waiting to see which one will die faster. Smart shot placement and positioning play a huge role in your vehicles success. 
Different ammuniton types are modelled ranging from AP to APCR and HEAT, Smoke rounds and HE. (with many more variants of shells) the performance of rounds is as real as possible.

The games weapon ranges (for vehicles) are scaled down to an X % of their real life counterpart, meaning for example 200 meters in game = 2k irl (not accurate, just an example) 



The game has many ways to control your units, most interestingly the First Person control mode which allows you to control units more akeen to a FPS game. 

Just a few days ago as of writing this (09.05.2024) GoH has released the German Infantry Overhual, the uniforms quality is the best on the market right now together with the huge amount of historical accuracy. Though accurate and beatiful the uniforms have some hiccups texture wise, not many but definetly noticeable by history nerds.
The Devs have said that Overhuals for Infantry will come to the other Factions too, that being: Finland and the USSR.



The Campaigns:
The base game is set in the "Ostfront" in other words the Eastern Front.
Included are 2 nations: Germany and Soviet Russia with their historic equipment and campaigns.

The game has recently received a completely new tutorial which is very informative and fun to play, teaching new players how to do almost everything.

The German campaign nicknamed "Ostfront" features 6 missions out of the box, those being:
- The Big Prize
- Back to Square one
- Among the Heavens
- Legend of Krasny Bor
- Ace of Swords
- In Spite of Everything

These missions are based on real locations which are faithfuly represented. 
The historical accuracy in these missions is to say the least a bit everywhere, though not completely made up, they sometimes simply just feel wrong.

The Soviet campaign nicknamed "Za Rodinu" also has 6 missions out of the box:
- Absolute Zero
- The Cold Supper
- Operation Bustard Hunt
- Unbroken
- Winter Storm
- Closing the Pocket

Same things can be said about these missions as was said in the German ones.

Also featured in the base game is the Conquest single or coop gamemode.
This gamemode offers the player the ability to research units via a progression system, and create their own Army.
Conquest revolves around researching units with points gained after each battle, these battles are divided into Attacking and Defending objectives on different maps, on the bigger "World" map. The goal, is to reach the enemy HQ. 
Many settings can be customized to the players liking including the length and strength of enemies forces.

This gamemode though great in theory, hasn't received much love from the Developers in a few years.
It is still a good choice for new players to learn and enjoy the game.



The Multiplayer:
Some would say, the main part of the game, Some say it's simply a sweat fest.

The gameplay in MP, is fine. The balancing isn't perfect in many departments, but it gets the job done if you want to play casually.
The biggest issue in MP, is sadly the performance, this mode suffers the most from bad performance and desync. 

It features 3 gamemodes: Battle Zones, Domination and the new Last Stand

Unlike previous games in the "series" GoH features a Doctrine system, Doctrines influence your Special Units and the Infantry units during the game.

I'm not the biggest fan of the mode, but if you like medium paced action and micromanaging.


That would be all for the Base game, it features hundreds of vehicles and equipment, lots of maps and many other interesting things.




The First expansion for the game was "Talvisota" this DLC brought the Finnish faction with it's own campaign ad equipment.
This DLC also introduced the Skirmishes, these smaller missions with objectives placed around the map to capture, capturing these unlocks new units for the player to use. These are also playbale in coop with friends.

the Finnish campaign nicknamed "Talvisota"
- Through Ice and Fire
- The Raate Road
- Stalins Big Guns
- Through the Fire
- The Northern Gambit
- The Bridge too Far

These missions are focued on controlling smaller infantry groups with limited amounts of Vehicles, the maps that shipped with this DLC are beatiful and plenty.




The Second expansion for GoH was the "Scorched Earth" DLC

This DLC incuded Additional missions to the base game German and USSR campaign

Ger:
- Siege of Sevastopol
- Battle of Narva
- Carpathian Turmoil
- The Final Offensive

Sov:
- Pavlovs House
- The Citadel
- Street to Street
- Konigsberg Couldron

This DLC also came with a new set of "Support"  Doctrines for USSR and Germany for Multiplayer.



The Final DLC and by far the biggest, being bigger than the game itself at release:
Liberation DLC 
Added the US faction with it's campaign and massive amounts of equipment, along with a German campaign set in the Western Front. 

Liberation camapign:
- Day of Days
- Hedgerow Hell
- Operation Cobra (Skirmish)
- Mortain Counterattack 
- Falaise Pocket (Skirmish)
- Hurtgen Forest (Skirmish)
- Hill 400
- Christmas Trouble
- Battle of the Bulge (skeemish)
- Lair of the Beast

The German part has the "Festung Europa" campaign:
- Hills of Saint Lo
- Operation Luttich
- Escaping the Pocket
- Wacht Em Rhein
- Blody Ardennes
- Last Stand at the Ruhr


This DLC, is the most detailed and added the most content to the game so far. 



And now for the Bad side of things in summary.
The game doesn't receive updates very often, mostly a few per Year.
It's been said to receive 1 Faction a year. (not exactly a bad thing)
The conquest mode hasn't received any major changes in a super long time.

This game runs on the GEM engine, which means it has many problems the older games have, these being:
- the AI is dumb as a rock, they can't really do their own thing and have to be babysitted all the time.
- the game has no servers, and relies on P2P (peer to peer) which means if the host lags, everyone lags no matter their settings.

OVERALL

I think this is by far the best WW2 RTS you can get. If you can get it on a discount, it will pay off very nicely.
Despite it's issues, the game is simply amazingly detailed and in depth.

Tons of problems that they refuse to change because of design intent. Devs are completely closed to feedback and argue in the forums and even result to childish name calling and gaslighting when confronted with legitimate feedback. Basic things are missing like machine guns shooting through fences, AP rounds through walls, all buildings being destructible (including single-story barns that should be destructible).

[h1] Inventory [/h1]
The inventory system is absolutely awful to deal with in an RTS, but putting up with it can give your infantry huge advantages (for example picking up a rocket launcher or replenishing grenades without spending resources). You would think they would implement a "scavenge" button or something, so you don't have to click on each dude and tell him to loot a specific dead guy, wait for him to run over to him, then manually take the grenades. But nope. No scavenge button, no resupply button. It makes dealing with the inventory a single-unit-at-a-time ordeal and not worth it.

[h1] Direct Control [/h1]
Direct control should be a selling point but is an absolute mess. Jiggle peaking and MG suicide bum-rushing are way too effective.

Direct controlling vehicles is really the only fun part. Direct controlling infantry is horribly clunky and way too effective, making it necessary but supremely unfun.

[h1] Multiplayer Skirmish [/h1]
No real spawn protection means it is absurdly easy to spawn camp since resource gain is logarithmic, and all your dudes spawn in the same place. Spawned units have an invulnerability period, but it doesn't help at all with the line of sight mechanics. The ambushers can just hide and wait for the invulnerability to end, and since they aren't moving and you are, they see you and you don't see them. Playing with friends means you need a ton of stupid house-rules to prevent spawn camping and MG suicide runs and the like that make the game silly and arcade-like.

There's no concede option. If you push someone back to spawn and cap all points, you have to wait for the timer to run down or leave (and then deal with remaking the lobby or reinviting the player). There is no option to just end it.

There's no ping map button?????????

Making a lobby is a pain. If you change any game option that is higher on the screen than options below that option, all options below it revert to default. This means if you want to change the war period after you've already set the resource cap or something, you have to go back and retype or select the drop-down option that you already changed. This is only one example of the ridiculous jank.

Unlike Company of Heroes, your resource gain does not change based on the number of units on the field, so you will always be gaining the number of resources determined by where you are on the resource curve (determined by match time and resource cap), even if you're maxed out on units. This is a key balancing mechanic in real RTS games.

[h1] AI [/h1]
AI is a joke. It blatantly cheats because it's too dumb to do anything other than run in a straight line. They get a ton more resources than you do in a match. It might seem cool to blast a million tanks with your one AT gun because the AI has a huge resource advantage over you, but it gets old real fast. Remember how resource gain is logarithmic? It doesn't seem to be that way for the AI. The AI continues gaining resources after you've hit your asymptote (soft cap), meaning you can't spawn units anymore, but they keep pumping them out. Your three tanks and AT gun can't compare to the fifteen they get in a match unless you're playing cheesy and direct control them. Cheese shouldn't be a game mechanic.

Absurdly overpriced to boot.

Very good RTS about the second world war. It needs some QOL fixes to truly shine, though.


[h1] Main gripes [/h1]
[i] (ok, more like all my gripes, haha) [/i]

[b] Building Things [/b]
[list]
[*]Laying mines requires micromanagement since the code isn't robust enough to automatically manage a squad laying mines. If you place multiple mines by shift left clicking, only one person will try to place them all. If you place multiple by right click dragging, Everyone will attempt to place mines, which is better, but they will usually leave half unplaced. Also you can't place multiple strips of mines by shift right click dragging.

[*]You can only make troops go to cover by clicking directly at cover. It's not possible to order your troops to seek cover or will they go to cover under free movement either, again requiring some extra micromanagement. If there was a way to make troops go to cover without having to find a convenient bush to click on would be great.

[*]Heavy Engineer Can't build gun emplacement if constructing building material dependent things first, and building it first doesn't use any building material. Maybe it is supposed to use an item but it is bugged? (it seems to use a special shovel, but sometimes this shovel is missing and the UI still shows one emplacement left. I guess this happens when I forget to resupply the heavy engineer squad in conquest. Confusing.)

[*]Unlike mines, engineer buildings are easy to build with multiple engineers but it is also too easy to accidentally cancel all your build orders by misclick or if your engineer dies. Maybe some kind of building interface would make building easier to manage. Maybe even add placing mines in there too!

[*]There's not enough time to prepare defenses in conquest.  forces have to be moved into defense positions from your side of the map, which after there is limited time to build anything. moving engineers with a truck it is possible to build one row of Tank Barriers that you right click dragged, but no time to place singular buildings in specific places before the opponent starts their attack (at 5 minutes of game time).
[/list]

[b] Ordering Units [/b]
[list]
[*]It's not possible to order multiple squads to move at the same time. It would help managing different attack direction tremendously if it was possible to group multiple squads and units together in different places of the front. Then have every group retain their formation and then you'd make a formation for the formations... yo dawg... I know, it's a lot, but then I could just push 1 for my alpha group and make them all advance, push 2 for bravo and angle them for support fire, press 3 to order mechanized charge, and 4 for support hotline and rain artillery fire! oh and 5 for bomber of course. Okay, artillery fits nicely to current group scheme since there is never too many artillery guns that wouldn't fit into one group.

[*]Can't order units through minimap. 

[*]Ordering tanks to move at the same time makes them move in a sparse column and not in a line or any other combat formation. So formations would be great. I liked those in Arma, but even one combat formation would nice.

[*]It's not possible to cue vehicle orders after ordering soldier to drive a vehicle (including artillery and ammo crates).

[*]Pathfinding isn't fully optimized yet. Everything works seemingly fine if there are no obstacles or the range is short. Even without obstacles on a longer path, the game chugs. If you surround an objective with impenetrable defense, the game can actually stop for a considerable amount of time when something tries to get in.

[*]Ordering a squad to repair a broken vehicle only makes one of the soldiers repair. Rest just watch from the side as one guy does it and even that guy gives up after one or too broken parts.

[*]Units won't fetch repair packs from close by enemy vehicles.

[*]Ordering artillery or ammo creates to move at the same time makes only one of them move initially. Maybe this is the vehicle column formation thing? Also, they end up in tight bunch at the destination no matter how you order them.

[*]Artillery have hard time moving in and out of trenches, requiring direct control and manually moving over the trench.

[*]Anything that isn't on foot gets stuck into everything often. So sometimes you will be wondering "Didn't I order a tank", and notice it stuck to some tree or another unit somewhere.
[/list]

[b] User Interface [/b]
[list]
[*]Many things lack hotkeys. For me, the hotkey bar is pointless since I constantly need to do everything. It actually would cost me more time to use the bar rather than just clicking through the numpad shaped menu (which can't be operated through numpad). Also, if you click between the buttons, your units will deselect like clicking ground.

[*]Inventory doesn't work in direct control. It opens but doesn't activate cursor, requiring to exit direct control and opening inventory again. In direct control, cursor activates only while examining bodies

[*]No hotkey for changing firearms (Grenades can be cycled with hotkey, though).
[/list]

[b] Misc. [/b]
[list]
[*]Sweeping for mines is very micro-intensive, slow and somewhat unreliable. You still have to pick those mines up since your units will still go through them if those mines are in the path.

[*]Crawling into or out of trench cancels direct control as a soldier.

[*]Maps in conquest are random. damage and defensive buildings don't persist between battles.

[*]No option to automate medics.

[*]Flamethrower infantry doesn't appreciate ROE. They just burn down everybody.
[/list]


[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

These things makes me hope for a fix constantly while playing.

Great game anyway. I have definitely gotten enough bang for my buck with this one.
