So after 398.6 of playing this game I can happily say that I love it and would recommend it to any RTS fan!

It took me a while to learn the ropes for this game as it can be daunting/difficult when you're first starting (So many mechanics and things to do!)

So to start off, I mainly play the dynamic conquest mode which is my personal favourite. The single player campaign missions are cool as well, but I kind of started off with the dynamic conquest and it's been my favourite since. 

In dynamic conquest you start by choosing which nation you wish to play us (Currently there's 3 nations, Germany, Soviet Union, Finland,  and I think there will be another faction in the future as a DLC)

When starting dynamic conquest, you get given a specific amount of resources/research points (Depending on what difficulty you select) You use these resources to buy the units you wish to take on your offensive/defensive missions and the research points you use to unlock new units when you're progressing your conquest campaign, so basically you start with standard infantry/early war tanks and you progress onto better/more elite infantry, more late-war tanks etc.
The amount of different units each factions has is crazy and that leads to so many different ways to play the game so the amount of replayability is pretty big! 

Obviously there are the cons as well, like issues with unit pathfinding (Sometimes you need to babysit a vehicle so it gets to it's destination as it might get stuck at a certain point)
The A.I could be better in terms of how they act/counter your playstile, although I can understand that making better A.I is no easy task and it depends on what game engine is being used and what limitations it has.
There could be some more additions to conquest, ie more special abilities as airstrikes/recon, etc and maybe even have some special tasks on some of the dynamic conquest missions to make it more varied (Like having to kill a specific high-value target or have a side activity where you need to destroy an enemy convoy).

The graphics are really great (At least for my eyes) Infantry models look nice, tanks are really detailed (They also change camouflage/uniforms depending on what season your battle is in, ie winter/summer) . The FX of explosions/smoke is great and the game has really nice destruction. You can blow up buildings, fences, telephone poles etc. The sounds and their quality is peak as well! Really makes you immersed in the battle! (Plus the devs are currently working on a sound overhaul/skin update which will get released in the future)

I've experienced many great moments whilst playing dynamic conquest.  One of my fave moments was me playing as the Germans on the attacking side, The main problem was me putting too much research points for better infanty/support units and not researching better tanks/at guns. So what happened was I capped the first attack point with my panzer pioneers and my 2 PZ3 tanks which was fairly easy. Had to defeat some standard Soviet infantry and some dudes with AT rifles. The Soviets sent some ZIS trucks with maxims as counters, but they were no match for my tanks and got annihilated pretty quickly!  Fast forward 10 mins from me capturing the point and I can hear the roar of a tank in the distance. Initially I assumed it was something like a T-70 which did not phase me at all, but 2 min later, I see my panzer 3 getting knocked out with 1 shot. I check the map, zoom in on the location and see that it's a f**ng KV-1 and I had no proper counter for it. The first thing I tried was driving around the KV-1's far side to get some shots off with my 2nd PZ3. Got a few shots in trying to break the tracks of the KV, but my attempt turned futile as it just deflected every shot of my PZ3. Seconds later, the enemy sent another reinforcement wave from the same side the KV came. It was a blob of infantry units which included some guys with AT rifles. My PZ3 got shocked by a few shots from the AT rifles, I tried to get away, but in the end my PZ3 got tracked and it was stuck. I had to watch as that KV-1 turned it's turret towards my paper PZ3 menacingly and I just accepted my fate. The PZ3 was knocked out with the first shot and none of the crew members survived. The KV then started to move towards my defensive position slowly. I was thinking of a way to knock it out, but was becoming desperate. I then remembered that my Panzer Pioneers had some guys with AT nades so I attempted to crawl around it's side while it was engaging my other units at the defensive position to try and disable it. It worked out, I got 2 guys with bundle nades to get on the right side of the KV. Threw the nades. First one did absolutely nothing and the 2nd one knocked out one of it's tracks.  The KV then turned to my 2 guys and gunned them down with it's MG. Brutal. At this point I was already thinking that it's GG as I had nothing to put up against it, but at  that point I also had a small moment of clarity. One of my panzer pioneers has a flamethrower! At that moment I knew what I had to do! Took 3 of my guys including the flamethrower to flank the KV1 from it's right side. Thankfully it had some bushes/foliage so the KV-1 did not see my guys crawling around it. I got 2 of my guys with rifles to distract the surrounding infantry and engage in a small firefight while I was directly controlling my flamethrower guy to crawl to the back of the KV-1. Once I got to the back of the KV-1 I started burning the crew man who was repairing the track and the engine compartment of the KV-1. After a long burst of flames I could see that the KV-1 caught on fire. Finally the whole tank went in flames. All the crew members crawled out of the tank burning and at last, the KV-1 was finished. All 3 guys including the flamer got killed afterwards as there was too much infantry surrounding the tank and they overwhelmed my 3 guys, resulting in their death.  All in all it was a difficult task to pull off, but when I did pull it off, it gave me an immeasurable amount of satisfaction and I just realised that even with an outdated army/units you can still find ways to deal with difficult situations in this game such as this one.  Bit of a long read, but just wanted to give a small story from my own gameplay which really made me appreciate the game so much more! 

All in all, just want to say a massive thank you to the developers as for me, this game is amazing with so much content to explore and I can't wait for any future updates/DLC'S!

Thank you for reading.

I do an in-depth review of one of my favorite franchise.
TLDR:
From "Men of War" the game this one replaces, overall there is Some improvement. The Men of War series, is the best WW2 RTS on the market, by far. But. they're moving towards microtransaction, and their DLC behavior is evidence for their lack of respect towards the community. 


"Uniquely. the game is a mix of RTS, Grand RTS, FPS and MOMBA, which if done well, would be incredible."

Soldiers Have Names, Inventories, and Experience  ::
You can move individual infantry units, which I greater prefer over 'CoH' and their squad based movement. In this I can split squads up and specifically move each solider to certain spots, or rearrange them into different squads. I can tell this solider to loot dead enemy soldiers, steal their grenades, switch weapons. There are also land mines, AT mines, trenches, foxholes you can dig. Conscripts don't start aiming great, veterans come loaded with AT, Smoke and AP grenades. Engineers can take petrol from a truck and refuel a tank, or use a detector to search for land mines, plant explosives. You can also control each unit yourself, by pressing 'E' you walk and shoot, either from a 3rd Person view, or from the normal RTS sky view. 

Big Tanks & Big Guns   ::
Tanks have realistic armor. Comparable to 'War Thunder' they have realistic armor on all sides and weak points to take advantage of. I can not speak on Historical accuracy, but I believe they are, at the least, very close. Realism mods on the Steam Workshop only add to its authenticity. Just like a solider, you can manually control tanks, tanks and guns also allow you to aim down a sight, as if you were in the tank. Artillery has its own unique angle as well. There are a huge amount of models for this game as well, every WW2 Tank 'War Thunder' has might also be modeled in this game. 

Campaign, Muliplayer and Conquest ::
The campaigns, unlike previous games, seem to focus a lot more on smaller based squads, more akin to 'Faces of War'. Only one mission out of six are genuine RTS missions. The rest are RTS/MOMBA quality style levels. There are also less factions then previous games in Campaign. Great Britain and Japan have been not made it into the campaign, only the USA, Soviet Union and Germany. The multiplayer is about as dead as any of the franchise games, occasionally there are players online, its not dead, its not busy. When it comes to 'balancing' there isn't much going on at all. They have tried to keep it real to WW2, and only set a few boundaries, like weapon range and supply amount. Unlike previous games, there is a new mode called Conquest, something slightly like a Grand RTS, where you decide where on the map the army will assault next, and a research tree to grow you army. Something like a basic 'War Band'. Multiplayer is really always been the best part of the games, because the computer is terrible.

The AI Nightmare  ::
It's so bad. Going all the way back to "Faces of War" I don't think the AI has changed at all. In Men of War Assault Squad 1 and 2 they didn't even have working AI in the skirmish modes. The enemy AI wouldn't have a single unit on the map. Unlike Skirmish or Conquest, Campaign is a built map, with each solider placed specifically and each reinforcement route planned manually. So there is an illusion that the computer is making decisions, when it's all planned out before hand. Practically, 99% of the time, you will start a conquest and never see a single enemy unit, the computer just doesn't work. It just does NOT work. On the 1% of times I have gotten it to work, the computer would send maybe 2 infantry squads and maybe 3 cheap tanks instantly to their death, or across the map, all bunched together. The computer has zero code written about this. Skirmish and Conquest, what ever they call it, the computer AI does not work. It doesn't understand you have a tank that is stronger and it doesn't understand any tactics or strategies. 
So the computer does Not work, but the AI? Pretty terrible too. Tanks, soliders, will ignore orders sometimes, or run into fire, take the longest way possible and gets stuck on a hill. Tanks AI switching APCR to HE while your in a tank battle. Other times you will be sending a tank or AT gun up to the front line, desperately needed, only to get stuck on nothing or stop randomly half way and by the time you realize it, your squad of infantry you were micro managing has been completely wiped out. You may ask a artillery gun to point in x direction or a a Zis truck to tow a DHSK to the front, again only to later find out the AI just couldn't do it. Sometimes the AI will shoot and kill its own team. 

A$$hole Greed  ::
When I first bought the game, the conquest and skirmish modes were the first thing I tried, I desperately was hoping they finally made a game with working AI, something akin to Starcraft. Boy was I wrong. I spent twenty minutes in an empty map, thinking the enemy was hunkering down, nope, same ♥♥♥♥ AI. Later I found out that Skirmish mode kinda worked, but you could only fight against the Soviet Union, which pissed me off, because that is faction  I  want to play as. To me, a long time Soviet player, maybe stereotypically, think the German faction is buffed up AI, and that the community is obssessed with Nazi's. I digress, I later found out that the Skirmish and Conquest modes were taken out of the game, and made a DLC that you now how to pay for. Not to mention that this game, had much more DLCs then previous, but unlike previous DLCs, the new ones were basic features that should be in the base game, lots of tank models and soliders that were in previous games, aircraft and a new faction and now skirmish. 

So let me reiterate using an analogy, they released a game in 2010 with two hundred models in it, twelve map missions and a broken skirmish mode. Now they release the same game with 50 models in it, 6 missions, and no skirmish, but you can buy all of those things as DLC, oh and the Skirmish is still broken. 
Wat ?    do   you   think   were   retarded  ? 


This game and the previous games have built such a strong cult following. We love WW2 and its history and love this RTS format, but this game really isn't worth it. Don't support this greedy f**k of a dev. Go buy Men Of War Assault Squad 2 on G2A.

This is the best and most fun WW2 strategy game you can play right now.  I got COH2 on sale a few years ago but have barely played it because there was always MOW Assault Squad 2 and now this to play, which for me are far more detailed and fun games with more tactics and much more depth to them. Really nice looking graphics, The atmospheric maps and weather conditions, great damage with vehicle combat and environment destruction, everything looks and sounds great, infantry combat is fun, tank battles are great, artillery is fun to use. This game is a really good improvement in so many ways from previous WW2 RTS games.

Singleplayer is great, loads to do, lots of the campaign missions are really good, and there are 3 campaigns for three different factions now, German, Russian and Finnish. Then there is the fantastic dynamic campaign where you can capture enemy tanks and vehicles and fight with them from battle to battle. Direct control is a great feature and playing co-op with friends who can command the tactical battle while you run around as an infantryman or drive around in a tank is a great development in RTS games. Developers are doing a great job and adding great new features to the game all the time so its going to get even better. Unlike most games the game comes with an editor so you can create new maps and missions yourself if you want. The new dynamic campaign and editor give infinite replayability, like Total War campaigns. Vanilla game is great on its own but on top of that there is a great modding scene and lots of excellent mods on the workshop, adding everything you want from endless new maps and new missions to many factions and units not in the base game.

I came to the game from MOW AS2  so the basic mechanics of control and how the game worked were familiar to me, but there are several new really useful mechanics and you have to learn them. There are issues here and there, like with all games, but many criticisms seem exaggerated, and devs are very responsive with ironing out any bugs. Its like saying the (older) Total War games weren't among the best strategy games ever because putting men on the walls of cities was often a bit ropey. To avoid frustration you do have to shepherd your vehicles a bit, can't always just click the other side of the map and expect them to find their way there safely if there are a lot of obstacles (and don't drive your vehicles too close together!) but jumping into direct control will usually get your vehicle out of any problems (shift and click to set a path is also often a good idea).  Doing the tutorial is maybe not the most fun way to learn the game, watching a youtube tutorial and jumping into playing the game is probably a more fun way.

Multiplayer is great, I've never had any technical problems playing the game, except sometimes on multiplayer, but it usually works fine even then, skirmishes online or co-op campaign with a friend is an especially fun mode. The DLC is also worth getting and adds a lot to the game, so I'd say getting it all in a bundle is the best way. COH1 was the best game back in the day but COH3 will likely have more simplistic gameplay like the others so personally I'm sure I will still prefer this game a lot over any potential competitors, Don't really know why anyone would skip a game this good on sale and wait for COH or MOW2 and rush off to pay full price as soon as they come out, when new games these days are almost certain to be a buggy mess for at least several months after release, if they don't turn out to be a total travesty.

So in summary, don't be put off by any negative reviews, (and the vast majority are overwhelmingly positive) its a 10/10 strategy game. Seems like the first new game I've seen which hasn't turned out to be a disappointment for a long time. If you look at it and think you will like this game, you will.

You might be familiar with Katyusha, but have you heard about her sister [spoiler]Andryusha[/spoiler]? That's how rich Arsenal in this game is. There is also a possibility in multiplayer to choose the period of war we want to fight in so we can fight with early war equipment without the need to deal with heavy tanks every single battle.

[b] Gamemodes [/b]

The campaign is pretty enjoyable as far as it is not a stealth mission. I don't know if it is just me, but I really can't stand them it is just a save-and-load game fest. Some defending missions on the other hand were truly epic and required a lot of tactical planning and micromanagement. Besides scripted campaign game offers dynamic campaign. It allows the player to choose a side, build a deck of units using the amount of money based on chosen difficulty and fight subsequent battles where you earn money and research points you can spend to unlock new units and even an airstrike. 

[b] New mechanics [/b]

As it is a Call to Arms DLC it naturally shares some similarities in in-game mechanics. There are 2 modes of direct control, It's possible to aim down sights in tanks, guns, and even with a sniper rifle. Interestingly enough those sights look different from each other. One little detail I am thankful for is when a soldier is carrying an AT weapon there will be an icon above his head. A cool addition is the possibility to build foxholes and to be honest you may disagree, but I am happy you cannot build long trenches lines like in Men of War: Arena they were to OP. Lastly, artillery is firing one shell at a time so you do not have to wait 2 minutes to reload and miss your target with quick 5 shots.

[b] Flaws [/b]

I did not encounter any major bugs and AI is not perfect, but much better than before, using cover could be improved as soldiers will always face the other way you want in the trenches. Path-finding is better, but could still use some work.

[b] Final verdict [/b]

All in all the game is great. I like it. 10/9.

128213979.review:
If you're a fan of games like Men Of War or the base Call To Arms, I have reason to believe you'll find this pretty enjoyable. My reasoning for why is that, in effect, GoH: Ostfront is a spiritual successor to Men Of War, as it covers the WW2 era that MoW also did, except on what seems to be a newer engine, with newer tech, newer systems, and a myriad of quality of life changes, also including mod compatibility and a workshop function pre-built into the game with a myriad of other improvements.

While I loved MoW, especially Assault Squad 2, it's safe to say those games have begun to show their age, and the jank present in them is both a result of said age and the older hardware and tech that they were made on. Ostfront doesn't have those issues, and the developers seem aware of what players enjoyed and disliked about MoW, as they're including the former and excluding the latter where they can. Things like better and automatic unit resupply, better ballistics and penetration calculations for tanks, better armor values and profiles, and smarter squad compositions are just par for the course. Alongside that, Ostfront not only includes the classic campaign and flag-capturing skirmishes that MoW was so well known for, but it also includes its own spins in the form of easily compatible multiplayer, co-op campaign functionality, and even a 'dynamic campaign' where you and an AI scramble to achieve military domination in a myriad of randomly selected battles where an evolving tech tree becomes available after the end of each turn.

Alongside this, while I do -not- agree with the choice of the devs to lock certain content behind DLC, such as the faction of Finland and all their units being locked behind the Talvisota expansion or certain iconic German and Russian units like the Karl Thor and certain special T-series tank variants being locked behind Scorched Earth, I do understand they're not a fully fledged AAA super development team and they have to pay the bills somehow. However, I also feel like it would've been better to just charge full price for Ostfront and then have all these DLC packs as free included content than stapling them on and asking for a dollar amount for each one, especially as that leads to cases where certain units that can be considered mandatory to the kind of experience MoW was so known for are permanently locked away unless you're willing to cough up the money, and you'll still have to fight these units in multiplayer if someone else owns the DLC. I played a match with a friend while someone on the other team was a Scorched Earth DLC holder and we had to watch one of our defensive positions get instantly nuked by a shot from the Karl Thor...Which we didn't have but they had because they paid money for it.

If you can overlook the faction/expansion-locked DLC content and approach this as what's basically a smaller-scale Men Of War successor that's focusing a lot more on an attempt at mixing quality and quantity to deliver an updated and revised experience that's far more tangible and satisfying? I think both RTS veterans and greenhorns alike are going to love this one, and players of Men Of War are going to feel right at home in this title while they're waiting for MoW2 to come out, and even then, Ostfront might prove to outpace MoW2 due to the sheer level of quality, effort, and dedication the developers have shown to keeping this thing going. We're at a year and a half since release and relatively sizable patches and updates are released on a month-to-several-month basis, they also talk to the community and are notably active on the discussion boards, so...

End verdict? I personally recommend it because it's a blast from the past that doesn't fail to deliver what it promises, and while I find the piecemeal approach to DLC irritating, it's not enough to turn me off of this. It's a classic from my childhood rebuilt and remastered from the ground up in painstaking detail, and I can't get enough of that. I will also personally say that, even despite my gripes, each expansion they launch does feel like it could be a $10 mini-game in and of itself, and I will begrudgingly admit I do still feel the quality and effort they put into each expansion justifies the price tag, as it keeps their lights on, their staff paid, and permits them to continue updating the game.

In an ideal world Ostfront would've had all factions and all campaigns in at launch, but Barbedwire aren't a huge studio, they don't have AAA money, or AAA resources, yet I'd say what they've made has put the new Men Of War to shame and outshines multiple other recent RTS releases.

So...Yeah. Give them your money if you want to, you'll be helping this thing thrive, and maybe if it sells well enough they'll just be able to make and release a sequel to Ostfront that has everything in it from the get-go.

It's very rare that I review a game, much less review it seriously. However, this game has quickly become one of my all-time favorites

[b] My perspective [/b] 
I do not come from a background of playing Men of War, as some players have. I have it in my library, but have yet to open it. However, I have played many other strategy games extensively, such as Company of Heroes 1 and 2, Blitzkrieg 1 thru 3, R.U.S.E., the Wargame Series, and bits of the Command and Conquer series So, this review comes from a completely fresh perspective on the franchise, but from a fairly experienced RTS perspective.

[b] Game Pace [/b] 
This game is, by far, the most enjoyable RTS I've played. It's realistic enough that knowledge of weaponry matters, but not so realistic that your infantry squad can be wiped out by a single soldier because you didn't invest enough in scouting & reconnaissance. It's a perfect balance, in my opinion, even as a vanilla experience.

[b] Control Individuals [/b] 
You can actually feel and hear the power of everything you use. This is only enhanced by the game's 3rd person feature, which is absolutely huge. Want to be the frontline soldier with an MG, holding off an attack? Take control of him while the rest of the battlefield continues to rage on. Want to take control of a tank or AT rifle to land that perfect hit on a weak spot? Press E, load Armor Piercing, and make sure your aim is true! It's a game were BOTH grand strategy and individuals matter, moreso than any other strategy game I've played


[b] Conquest & Co-Op [/b] 
I have very minimal experience playing multiplayer, just because the singleplayer dynamic campaign (called Conquest) is so good! You can set your difficulty, and play persistent battles which determine your resources, as you make choices on what vehicles and equipment to research to best counter the equipment that the AI, too, is fielding. And the best part? It's co-op too! You can play with up to 3 more friends as you allocate resources, and work together with the decisions you make in each and every battle.

[b] Critique [/b] 
My only criticism is that the AI isn't perfecty up to snuff. There are occasional points of gameplay where you do feel as though you have to micromanage. In my experience, this mostly occurs when towing equipment such as artillery. Parts of the game are physics-based, and sometime the AI isn't smart enough to avoid driving full speed over a crater, or not cut corners on a bridge, sending the towed piece to a watery death. 

[b] Workshop Support [/b] 
One thing to also note, this game has a huge workshop. Most EVERYTHING has a mod. If you don't like how one aspect is, there's a mod for it! AI pathfinding, new nations, full conversion mods, construct-able buildings, conquest maps and call-ins. You name it, someone has changed it and it's on the workshop!

[b] Rating Out of 10 [/b] 
Overall, a solid 11/10 from me, and I hope the devs continue to get more and more support to develop this amazing game.

[h1]TL;DR!!!!! Overall: 8/10 for extremely atmospheric and good gameplay paired with an incredible map line up and the addition of a solid campaign, great dynamic campaign, great amount of maps, and good unit variety. If you continue to read, you'll see that most of the game play elements are on the positive side while most of the technical things are on the Con. *if you are simply wondering if you'll enjoy this game, Im sure you will.* [/h1]

I want to give a clear review on this game because you either have people up voting with no real flesh to their reviews or people down voting over emotion more so actual reasons.

Gates of Hell feels like a "better" MoW: AS2. It literally does. The base game runs significantly better and also looks better at that. The sound design is great and in my opinion, it is more atmospheric than Call to arms and MoW. A lot of that has to do with the units themselves. Better animations, death animations, unit chatter, etc. Ill give a list of pros and cons so people who actually are on the fence about this game can pick what will or wont break them.(waited almost a year to get this due to dodgy reviews.
----------
PROS(updated):
-Atmosphere is amazing 
-Campaign is engaging 
-Good unit variety at this point
-Graphics
-Sound design
-Unit animations/death animations are great
-Sound track is a bit above average but still on the good side
-Plays like a "better' MoW:AS2. Which is like 5points in itself
-Dynamic campaign....Literally the best feature in the game imo(think of it like galactic conquest. same principle)
-Dynamic campaign is also coop
-VERY good unit variety.
-Units like the field engineer have great abilities that literally transform the battlefield. Don't forget to use them
-Call to arms direct unit control
-Free Updates that add this such as new units and maps
-Campaign mission line up is insane with the DLC and is going to require many-many hours to finish.



CONS(updated):
-I know this is taking place in the Ostfront Portion of the war, but the only factions are Germany, Russia, and the Finnish And that makes sense. Nevertheless, still only 3 factions unless you use the Valor mod.

-The AI at times could be considered brain dead. Mostly when it comes to grenades. Not game breaking like many reviews here say. But noticeable 

-Although devs have said other wise, the AI seems to have a large advantage over your resources and troops. Often leading to unfair matches. They seem to always have waves of troops. This does not mean you can not win, it just feels like you are in the battle of the bulge as the Americans if you know what that is. Often does make the matches feel more engaging tho. Just a bit too often.

-The AI seems to have better aim than your troops. Notably with tanks

-This game is a bit more micro-managy compared to MoW. But that's also because it feels more like squad or platoon based than whole army based. Which is sort of a good thing(yes you can 100% still make very large armies)

-The mods are NOTTTTT as good as MoW's or even Call to Arms....at all...not even close....what so ever.

-Price is high for no reason
-UI isn't the best but its workable

-I personally have seen some things about bugs. At the time of writing this I have not encountered any worth talking about. But glitches are a con either way

-And the most important one. This game is locked behind a pay wall which is call to arms. Call to arms is objectively a worse game that GoH and has considerably less content, yet you are forced to buy it. GoH also is its own separate entity and has nothing to do with Call to Arms. Its even downloaded as its own game. I assume this was done for the same reason Infinite warfare was paired with COD4 remastered. It was done as a way to get people to buy both games as they know Call to arms is not great. I also want to point out that many of this game's issues stem from the fact that this is basically on the same engine as Call to arms. This engine is considerably more unstable than MoWs in terms of its functionality and that also brings the issues I mentioned above such as the bad AI and things.
----------
MIXED(updated)
-Im moving DLC from CONS to MIXED. The addition of the new scorched earth DLC adds a very good amount of play time and content to the game. Add that along with the first dlc, and the mission content alone is outstanding !! Reason im putting this as mixed instead of PRO still lies in the fact that this inherently is "DLC for a DLC" and the pricing of the first DLC. Once again, price is a big factor with this game because of the up front cost of having to buy Call to Arms to even play. So while I understand that devs need to make money and put alot of time and effort into dlc, it ultimately still is a factor to consider. If you bought these games on sale then great! We are in a better position than most. But I'm sure a large portion of the players did not get GoH or the DLC on sale. This is the first time the game and the dlc has gone on sale for any reasonable price. I DO recommend the DLC as the content is very solid nevertheless. Not to mention future additions. Remember, this is a review on the game to game enjoyment. Nothing extra
----------
NOTES
A few things such as multiplayer I can not speak on yet as I have not played it yet. From what i've heard, the connection is better than MoW and Call to arms but ill update when I play it. I also am not going to talk about other issues with the devs such as them being accused of ignoring their player base and hiding active criticism. I don't know enough about that and I personally don't think it takes away from your match-to-match enjoyment of this game. Which is one of the reasons im writing this review as its based off of the game itself and none of that extra stuff.

While I know its hard, It is best to go into this game not thinking about Call to Arms. It has nothing to do with that game and is not connected to it whatsoever outside of being required to play it. *so if you did not like call to arms, that does not mean you will not like this game at all*. Its nothing but a handicap and irritating pay wall(In relevance to GoH). It is more comparable to MoW:AS2 which is why you see it everywhere in the reviews. 
----------
Overall: 8/10 for extremely atmospheric and good gameplay paired with an incredible map line up and the addition of a solid campaign, great dynamic campaign, and good unit variety

I DO NOT recommend buying this at full price. Reason being is its too close to MoW in terms of it being a WWII tactical RTS(even if I consider it to have better gameplay). MoW has VERY established mods which are not on GoH and are never coming to it. Which automatically means MoW has more content. Hopefully GoH gets more content as it ages as it is still fairly new. I can not justify buying this a full price for that reason paired with call to arms being required.

So much promise. So disappointing.  Feels unfinished and improperly play-tested.
Like
*Unit detail and variety
*Conquest mode – ongoing army that progresses.  Great concept.
*Control options. (not execution of said options though)
*Repairing and scavenging equipment.

Dislike
*Campaign
*Many of the maps are dull.  Particularly for conquest.  Very few interesting positions to assault or defend.  Very little variety in buildings.
*Graphics average at best.
*Brightness not adjustable. 
*Load times pretty bad.
*Many things blend into landscape too easily.  Hard to pick out.
*Infantry vulnerability.
*Buildings are all just hollow boxes and if there are two windows can be shot straight through.  Infantry are difficult to order into buildings.
*Infantry do not place themselves in cover very well.  Often must be done one by one which is fiddly and takes too much time.
*Line of sight & fog of war seem completely broken.   If the AI has one unit that can see you then all of their units can with no seemingly no accuracy penalty.  Range seems to be so long as to be basically limitless.  Indirect fire has insane accuracy. AI seems to find a way to one-shot you through the eye of a needle (e.g. through the windows of a building).  
*Conquest – progress is basically irrelevant as crews cannot be moved to new equipment as it becomes obsolete.  Also, infantry vulnerability means there is little point in getting invested in progress.
*Conquest – Defence. Positions given are often poor.  No time given to set up defences.  Why always two points?  Why not one? Why not five? Would be awesome if the player could select the position. Why not? It’s the players territory after all.
*Conquest - Balance of difficulty levels.  Sometimes ‘easy’ is very easy and sometimes offers quite a challenge. ‘Normal’ scales up far too quickly for equipment available.  Enemy seems able to spawn many more units.
*Control scheme is fiddly and annoying.  
*The direct control mode really can’t be used much as this then leaves the rest of your army without oversight and often it’s impossible to see much – when left in AI mode they will shoot at things you can’t see in direct control mode.  Generally I only used it when I couldn’t move a unit into position (see next point).
*Movement of stationary weapons (AT guns, mortars etc) is impossible if an enemy has been spotted nearby as they will automatically drop out of movement mode constantly.  Direct control seems to be the only way.
*Friendly fire.  Your troops will just fire at the enemy regardless of friendly troops in front.  Made worse by the fact that you can’t fix facings of stationary weapons – they will suddenly swing around and shoot at enemies on the other side of friendly troops.
*Placement of sandbags is very difficult (unless you are placing a single one).  Very tricky to join them together.  Would be better to just have a smaller sandbag ‘unit’ that you can then just drag into a line as long as you need.  Can’t join large foxholes together.
*Repairing is a bit painful as you have to keep telling them do each part.  They should just keep repairing until it is finished or they run out of repair equipment.   Impossible to tell how many repair boxes or whatever they are called will be required to complete the repair.
*Impossible to know how far weapons will fire.  No range cones, even if the developer does not want to do this for some kind of realism reason they also give no range information on equipment.  Weapons will not move to get in range to carry out an attack order.  They will do it if they’re in range, they won’t if they’re not.

Game has amazing potential and I've tried to force myself to enjoy it, however I just can't.
CONS
The SP campaign is short and the missions are the same formulaic "throw a billion enemies at you" formula. The games performance is horrible and has sometimes crashed the entire PC. Multiplayer performance is abysmal, granted you even get into a game trying to use any mods, as even if you are running the same version of the mod it will still show a "Resource Desync Detected" error. Have to lower the graphics (in multiplayer only) to low even though i'm on a pretty high end pc, or else the game freezes often. (also horrendously long loading times.) Tiny details make no sense such as the star on soviet caps being completely reflective, and modelling insides of tanks you will never see, also hamper performance on MP, despite the graphics of the game not being that good. There is also far less environmental destruction compared to Men of war assault squad 2's. Game is too unpredictable with fog of war (even though it is the correct way to play) that i usually have it off as your soldiers can only see about 10 feet in front of them. Enemy AI is also usually too easy. AI also will do annoying flanks with something like 3 men which are just annoying to kill. Then the devs release two more individual DLC's while there are mods such as valor that do exactly what the DLC's do. Every update they seem to reduce the range of artillery/anti tank guns, which allows enemy tanks to snipe you without being able to shoot them back. None of the maps really feel unique, there are usually no good spots for cover except for the same old trench on a hill overlooking an area, I would much prefer more environmental cover. 
PROS
Healing system is far greater than Men of war. Units no longer need to kneel to bandage themselves (usually would end up getting them killed) Resupply system is also better.
The gray, dark coloring in the game is very fitting for the eastern front. 
UI is cleaner and better to use
I prefer the construction from combat engineers, with sandbags and hedgehogs, however MOWAS2 had better minelaying mechanics. They are very tedious in CTAGOH.

10/10, Resource Desynchronisation detected.

Call to Arms - Gates of Hell: Ostfront is an abomination to gaming and to the history of the human race. Do not buy this game for your own health.

GAMEPLAY:
Soviet bias is common throughout World War Games but no game illustrates the pure boner bias this game has for Stalin's little Red Army. Tanks in this game are truly works of art that the eyes of humans can't even comprehend most of the missions consist of defensive objectives where you sit there for an hour and a half, shooting armor-piercing rounds from tanks and Anti Tank guns sometimes even howitzers as armored Goliath after armored Goliath are blown to smithereens. But once the KV-1 enters the battlefield it's all over. This game has the most realistic tank combat ever seen by humans which makes actual WW2 veterans keel over from the pure PTSD it ensues in them. Sometimes the average Russian tank can withstand AP hits which no tank could ever survive or such heavy bombardment from HE that you'd think the tanks crew's brains would be a red soup but no these tanks continue their communistic wrath on your German troops with such rage and impunity it seems the time of the 1000 year Reich would end at that moment. But after you enter 20 AP rounds into the most basic tank that was probably put together by starving Ukrainians the tank and its crew are nothing more than a smoldering ruin. but the KV-1 is Thanos. the endgame. the destroyer of worlds. I have more PTSD from fighting KV-1s in this game than actual WW2 Vets who fought on the Eastern front do. I've seen the KV-1 take at least 50 AP rounds, 100 HE rounds, and 2 direct Howitzer Rounds and the Iron Beast continues to destroy the entire German line by itself even if you disable its tracks the monster of steel will murder your entire family because it simply can not die. I sat there for probably a whole hour using every Anti-tank method I had and Stalin's metal fury continued to rage. Tank combat in this is a horrible experience I wish for no one to experience.

The Mission Design of Ostfront is truly something special. the story consists of two campaigns the Germans, and the Soviets, and with the Finnish DLC you get to experience the wonders of the Winter war (Don't buy it). I won't get into the specifics of every mission because to be honest I try to forget I ever played them (I'm mentall unwell due to this games mission design).

 The German Campaign
 mainly consists of Defensive missions against the Soviets, you see some Iconic Eastern front battles like the Battle of Kursk, well you see the aftermath of Kursk you don't actually get to witness the actual interesting part of the battle. Most Defensive missions are pretty similar you have a set amount of time to prepare your defenses which tend to be a mix of Anti-tank weapons and tanks that haven't seen combat since Tsar Nicholas was still in power. you are also typically given Anti tank mines which rarely work, sometimes Enemy tanks will perfectly dodge the mines as if they knew they were there or they just drive right over them completely unharmed. Offensive missions tend to be relatively similar you are typically attacking a much stronger force and you almost always end up having to steal their equipment to fight off their tanks or any reinforcements they send to stop you. almost every mission follows a very similar path there are a few missions which leave this path but those missions tend to be the worse and the most broken. Even though Digitalmindsoft is a german company and Barbedwire Studios is an international company they apparently couldn't find a single german to voice act their game, so most of the dialogue (If it is even voiced) is some poor man speaking english attempting to do a german accent.

The Soviet Campaign
This amazingly designed campaign starts off with soviet POW's being transported by the Germans until they are ambushed by Russian Partisans. After your transport truck magically loses control of the steering you and the rest of your Russian comrades must loot the dead Germans and proceed to take out an entire platoon of Germans with barely any equipment and even less medics. this mission sucks. it doesn't help that the half assed control a unit system barely works and as you attempt to 360 no-scope faze clan the Germans with their own guns you end up dying because the green marker is a lie and the Germans play Apex Legends. The rest of the Soviet Campaign is similar to that of the German, poorly made Defensive and Offensive missions where you don't even participate in actual interesting battles that took place in the Eastern front no you attack some random German Convoy or you sit on a road for 3 hours as you protect your own convoys from the entire population of Berlin with a few guys and two anti tank guns, yes that's a real mission. The Soviet Campaign also has a few dialogue bits but its voice acted by the exact same German dude who even still has his German name of Hauptmann. 

The Finnish Campaign: Talvisota
The Finnish Campaign bravely starts off with a defensive mission as the outnumbered and outgunned Finns attempt to hold their ground against the wrath of the Soviet Union. the rest of the campaign consists of poorly made offensive and defensive missions where you barely beat the Russian forces as you are always outnumbered and outgunned which makes sense the Soviet Union was far stronger then the Finns. But try taking out a KV-1 with a WW1 tank and a few Molotovs its a great experience. The last mission of the Finnish campaign consists of the Finns attacking a German occupied bridge. Yes the Germans. You thought this was about the Finnish fighting the Soviet Union? WHAT? no the Germans who by the way are the ones supplying the Finns which is why they have almost entirely German equipment. Although the Finns did fight the Germans in real life in 1944, this mission gives zero context as why our enemy switched randomly from the Soviets to the Germans. The DLC is 18$ which is a lot of money for a few re-skinned assets and a few missions which suck. The DLC also has Dialogue which isn't voiced at all, not even the great Team Switching German could make his return. 

EDIT: LIBERATION DLC: 
Not much changes in this DLC that makes the rest of this game hot garbage. you know how half the German army is off fighting and dying in Russia? or how the germans were unprepared for the allied landings in Normandy? or how they couldn't call in reinforcements to Normandy because good ole Fuhrer Adolf was taking a nap? well that doesn't matter because although the entire allied forces are supposedly right behind you. You are given a singular squad for most of the missions and two pieces of armor or artillery to fight against the entirety of Germany. The Missions were poorly designed for the american side and not much changes for the Krauts. The German missions are slightly better due to the fact that you are mostly defending which makes sense. half the missions in this dlc are poorly designed capture the flag missions with no real depth and definitely not worth the price. oh and have fun invading Normandy with like 5 dudes.

THE HISTORY
For a World War 2 game that takes place on the Eastern Front we barely see any significant battles we see Kursk but only the last tidbits of the battle and we spend it searching for a singular downed pilot. that's right an entire German Platoon wastes their men and armor to find a singular German pilot after one of the most devastating battles for the Germans during the Eastern Front. The Soviets aren't much better the only good thing about their campaign is that we don't have to fight KV-1's. We also see no significant battle during this campaign. The Finnish Campaign is no different only that we randomly switch over to a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bridge mission where we fight the germans.

Save your money don't buy this game its horrible and I need to see a therapist after playing it. I don't know why I wasted my time writing this.

123346790.review:
This game is good with the potential to be great with some bug fixes and quality of life improvements.

Whats Great:
The feel and power of all the units.  Every gunshot, mortar round, tank shell feels as if it has weight and will potentially kill you.

Pulling off a great attack.  When your squad finally makes it to that objective storming through the gunfire with a well pulled off smoke barrage and suppressing fire it feels great.

The game play loop is fantastic, and we keep on coming back to play co-op AI skirmishes.

Taking direct control of the units to pull off just the right shot is a good time.  And being able to split infantry into fire teams allows you a good level of options for how to approach a problem.  Looting is also fun, especially in the dynamic campaign where you loot carries with you.

Whats Meh:
AI Pathing  - Trucks will run into one another while using roads, sometimes just getting stuck, other times exploding in easily avoidable head on collisions.  Other times you tell an infantry squad to move and they will just stick there and only some of the squad will move from their position as a grenade plops inbetween them.

You cant load or tow man packed weapons...if the machine gun is on a chassis or its two guys lugging the mortar...they gotta walk it up the whole way instead of riding in a truck.  And when you DO tow a gun sometimes it gets stuck in a state where it can't be untowed.

Looting in the dynamic campaign is tough....as the weapons only reloads are what you scavenged in the last game for infantry, and doesn't get restocked in between maps or reloaded from ammo crates, and micro managing that in the middle of a mission can be a hassle.

Some general instability problems with game crashes (using an AMD card).


All in all I would definitely recommend this game despite its flaws, and if all of those do eventually get resolved, this will be an Amazing game.

122516217.review:
[h1]I Hope Relic is Taking Notes [/h1]

This game always popped up in my feed given that I've flushed over 6k hours of my life into CoH2. I'd always blown it off because, from what little I knew about it, I assumed it was one of these disjointed RTS/FPS hybrid/milsim sorta joints that was probably for players looking to get the best of both worlds as opposed to actually experiencing a fully fledged and highly rigorous RTS experience. This assumption was founded mainly on my understanding of the original Call to Arms. Well... nothing could be further from the truth. 

Not only is this game perhaps more fully fledged than most other RTSs ever made, the integrated "FPS" elements aren't merely some gimmick aimed at appealing to a broader audience. [b]The direct control mechanic, which is actually not in first-person, introduces an entirely new stratosphere of tactical potential that launches the game into a league of its own.[/b] For instance, in Company of Heroes, micromanagement and spontaneous combat events do require the player to home in on the utility of one unit at a time in order to accomplish specific goals. However, the RNG element of this system still distances the player from being able to fully assert their tactical dominance over engagements. Being able to get down and dirty, and execute plays EXACTLY how you want to, is not only extremely thrilling, but mentally engaging. Nothing is more satisfying than landing a hit on the ammo box of a Konistiger from across the map and watching its turret literally blast off into space while the ravaged crewmen flail around engulfed in flames. The level of detail, being able to manage the precise inventories of each unit, being able to choose the exact window you'd like a unit to fire from, being able to dictate the stance you want a unit to take on (prone, knee, standing), needing to tend to medical supplies, repairs, munitions, and all these aspects of the game's world which make it come alive, one questions how much more they may possibly be immersed into an RTS experience. 

[i]There are an infinite number of potential solutions to every problem. There is no way of predicting what's going to happen next. There is always more you could be doing to get an edge. The difference between victory and defeat is often a mere well placed smoke grenade or an extra med pack. That bush in the corner may prove the perfect vantage point for your AT rifleman to bring down an enemy heavy tank. And no Company of Heroes moment compares to being able to directly control a flamethrower infantryman as he torches a a tank's engine, forcing the crew inside to flee their vehicle and throw themselves on the ground, begging for mercy. We need more eyes on this game. We need to push it to the forefront so that the multiplying number of RTS developers seeking to make their mark on this new age for the genre can gain true respect for what Barbed Wire Games has accomplished here. They must recognize that to deliver on a product that's anything short of what Gates of Hell represents would be to only take another step back into those failures which are to blame for the decades long death of our genre out of which we are on the cusp of emerging from.[/i]

121497696.review:
The game is pretty solid, but it does have it's problems. The problems are mostly minor, like pathfinding issues on some maps, but I've found that after more than 1,000 hours playing, the majority of people's complaints are based on "realism". This game does look beautiful, and while many aspects of it are "realistic" it doesn't feel like it was actually meant to be a simulator. GoH sits somewhere between an RTS like Company of Heroes and a more serious and realistic battle simulator.  It has some really nice features that are absent from other RTS games, like the ability to take over any individual soldier or vehicle in FPS mode, the ability to play the dynamic campaign in co-op mode, and other features which set it apart. The point of a game is to be fun and entertaining, and this game is definitely that. It does have it's flaws which are not deal breakers for the majority of people, but I've been on the Dev's Discord for months and seen firsthand that they do in fact patch bugs and gameplay issues while also releasing additional content. So, this game is much like most games in the sense that it's still under development while having been released, but it's also extremely easy to mod this game so if there's a particular way you'd prefer to play it, you can learn to mod it in under an hour and start changing whatever you want, even adding whole new vehicles to the game. Personally I give GoH a 7/10 which is pretty high praise from me.

EDIT: Next month I'll hit 5,000 hours in-game, I've been an official beta tester, and I've created multiple huge mods for the game. The content that's still being released, the new game features, the care and maintenance fixes still being released, and the continuing expansion of a game originally called "Ostfront" that now includes the West front too... well it's safe to say that even with the minor wonkiness of the game, it's still very satisfying to play, even after thousands of hours.

This game is a shockingly good time. There's definitely an adjustment period where you need to re-learn how to play its bespoke approach to RTS (combing tactical, mil-sim esc top down combined arms combat with intense third person shooting), however once you're over that hump it's consistently fun and insanely impressive.

It's really hard for me to have quite as much fun playing other RTS games now knowing I can't just jump into a soldier and deliver a battle defining anti-tank grenade into the ass end of something someones been saving up all game for.

While the campaign cut-scenes are a bit janky and there's bugs here and there, overall it's an extremely impressive title.

There's heaps of content for both chilling out on the weekend in conquest mode or jumping into MP battles with friends, and the skirmish maps are an absolute blast with some major challenges that we'll gladly grind out for an entire Sunday for the hope of victory.

To any of my friends who haven't picked it up yet and see this, pick it up ASAP I can't wait for you to experience it!

This game is everything I loved about Men of War Assault Squad 2 and everything I disliked about it with some new additions to the list. This game really feels like a sequel to the Men of War games than an addition to CTA, which I like, but in keeping with the franchise it is definitely a micromanagement simulator. If that is what you are looking for then look no further. If you prefer a higher level strategy then steer clear. This review only covers the single player skirmishes and campaign since I don't have multiplayer experience with this one.

Pros:
This game retains the same familiar feel of MOWAS2, but with better graphics and larger maps (benefit of coming from CTA). If you know how to MOW then you generally feel comfortable with this one. There are some large battles that are amazing that really need tactical level strategy to achieve the objectives or survive. The explosions are satisfying and using combined arms to achieve the goals feels satisfying.

Cons:
The pathfinding for the AI seems to have gotten worse over the years. It is worse than MOWAS2. There should be improvement over time, not digression. Telling a soldier to look in a crate 2 feet away suddenly becomes a headache because there is a fence post in the way and he gets stuck. It happens constantly. Telling a squad to traverse a section of battle field while you issue some other orders? Better not do that since you will have to babysit the squad cause some will get stuck somewhere. Next, the objectives have never been more unclear. Defend the village you say? I didn't know I had to take my only 6 soldiers and have them search the far reaches of the map to kill every last soldier in an enemy battalion to trigger the next phase of the mission. Also, the voice overs have random glitches where they don't match the messages or repeat when they shouldn't. Lastly, and this is just a personal issue, why are we still throwing these random sneak missions into a tactical combat strategy game? I hate sneak missions.

Aside from these issues it is a solid tactical strategy game that I will continue to play (skipping past the sneak missions) If you like micromanagement in your strategy, this is for you. If you want a higher level of strategy where the sub-units can make some decisions, then there are plenty other titles in this genre that offer that experience.

Gates Of Hell is a great game. The best WW2 RTS around. If you think you will like a hardcore WW2 RTS you should try it. Especially on Steam sale. 

First things first, The DLC thing needs to be addressed. For once this is nothing to do with "Greedy Devs" as the seemingly "most helpful" review inaccurately describes the "DLC" situation. They are different developers from CTA. They were forced to tie their game to Call to Arms to even get it released, to get the use of the Engine licence of CTA. That's it. And you should be glad they succeeded in releasing this excellent game. This is a game made largely by Modders of MOWAS2 so they are making the game they want, and that a lot of us want, not as dictated by actual greedy Dev companies. There is a longer explanation someone else wrote before at the bottom of this review for those interested in any more details. If you like the look of this game you should get it. See it as purchasing Ostfront for £15 currently on Steam sale and completely ignore CTA. You don't even have to install CTA.
 
This is a much better game than COH2 for anyone who enjoys a bit of realism in their games. The armoured and vehicle combat is a lot of fun, as is infantry combat, and artillery and all the explosive battles and environment destruction works brilliantly together, as you can hide you men in shell holes created by artillery.
If you have no patience and want arcadey stuff you may not like it. If you have the patience for MOW Assault Squad 2, this is a considerably updated version with better graphics and many improved features, like medics being able to heal while crawling and thus not getting shot, improved direct control, more fortifications and much more. They have been adding a lot of free content in updates since last autumn, and working on the new DLC so people can't really complain about content, and, being made by modders, it is one of the most modding friendly games out there now, so there is lots of extra free content if you want it, you are free to create your own with a great editor included in the game, and there will be much much more.

The Finnish DLC is excellent. It is really the first DLC to the base game Gates of Hell: Ostfront. It adds a lot of content, an extra faction with a lot of new units. lots of excellent missions and is  worth it for its size. I don't feel like I'm getting ripped off for content like this. It feels more like the good old days of gaming when an expansion pack was rare and really added a lot. Something like medieval 2 Total war Kingdoms back in the day. Ostfront feels like good games being worked on and made better, unlike the last 10 years of gaming where it seems almost all game companies were determined to take great concepts and franchises and make them worse, dumb them down for the masses and ruin them, while ripping off their customers.

So I think most people who aren't put off by the difficulty will really enjoy this game. For ordinary play it feels at least as finished as MOWAS2 ever did, much more so in fact, and has felt in this finished state for playing since last autumn at least. More gamemodes will be coming out and many existing aspects refined of course. The more complex controls can be a bit fiddly at times but most of the time in ordinary combat it is fine, for those of us who like the complex mechanics of games like Arma and MOWAS2 that is nothing new, and there is hope for even further improvements. The game looks and feels amazing, it is definitely the best game of it's kind, and I think you will be missing out if this is your type of game and you don't give it a try.

The masses will no doubt run off and give all their money to actual greedy mainstream developers and huge games companies turning out an inferior product as usual. I think people are being unfairly predjudiced against the game by the DLC label, and stupid reviews. I felt some correction was necessary. "How is it attached to the atrocious 'CTA'? Well, I'll educate you after some research of such a poor marketing decision: the original developer, Digitalmindsoft, was rejected by the Men of War publisher to produce Men of War 2, sidelined for a team to develop 'Men of War Arena' (which predictably failed miserably, now being converted in a failed state to MOW2) as a shoddy mobile-esque direction...likely to explain their absurd direction with the base CTA (publisher pressure for that deplorable P2W market).

Fortunately, the developer, Digitalmindsoft, decided to be independent as some pride in their development integrity - probably sick of being overlooked or coerced into incompetent, absurd projects. They adopted some experienced modders as 'Barbedwire Studios' - in progress already with GOH - who were in a stalement without any legal rights to the engine - their whole development at risk. Subsequently, they begun to support releasing 'Gates of Hell' as unable to produce a sequel to Men of War, but here's when the politics starts - it was created with the engine of their former overlords, 1C Entertainment, who wouldn't license the use of it any more. Consequently, they had the license of the engine via 'CTA' and so attached it to this as a contrived 'DLC' on a technicality, even as a horrible handicap and inevitably going to cause prejudice... The end result, however, proves they were absolutely a threat to their former masters and more than capable in vision - this is a brilliant product only restricted from how it's delivered...as a legally necessary DLC for an awful base game."

117161937.review:
I want to start this review by saying that I have been a fan of men of war for over 10 years, I have just about every game and ~1500 hours in MOWAS2 alone. I understand that those games too were plagued with some weird design choices and stupid AI. I would also like to say that I do like this game, I think it's fun and I will continue to play it and (usually) enjoy it. The models and textures are very well done and add a lot of flavor, the voice lines are well done, and the campaign is really fun. It is genuinely probably one of my favorite games at the moment.

However, it is plagued with some serious issues that really should not be a problem this late into development. The AI seems to have slightly more "realistic" pathfinding than Men of War, the vehicles take roads and so on, but if you aren't constantly paying attention to your units and micromanaging them then they will more often than not get stuck on some random entity, which is something that did happen in MoW but not nearly as much as it seems to happen in this game. Half the time if I order my towed artillery to move somewhere they don't even move and I have to enter direct control and do it myself. The AI also does not fare well in combat, units often don't engage in combat even when ordered and when using the attack ground option with artillery I sometimes have to do it 5 or 6 times before they actually listen or even do it in the direct control mode because they just refuse. Infantry combat is mostly up to RNG, and at times even your experienced infantry can repeatedly miss their shots while a random Soviet partisan domes your squad leader in the head with a rusty mosin. On top of that, if infantry is engaged while moving they will often just keep sprinting into the enemies line of fire and all get gunned down. It doesn't help that in multiplayer, people are really sweaty (obligatory "skill issue") and it is borderline unplayable for anyone who is playing against someone who memorized every single hotkey meanwhile you just got home from work and want to relax and play a game.

There are a lot of issues with the AI and those are just some of them, but I feel the need to explain that with heavy scripting, the game is perfectly fun. For me, I play a lot of the single player missions or ♥♥♥♥ around in the editor and the issue is usually when I decide to play multiplayer, skirmish, or conquest that the game can get extremely frustrating (again, skill issue). Firstly, why is there no reverse option for vehicles? It is really annoying when I have to micromanage all of my infantry from getting killed by a single HE round and at the same time I have to slowly right click right behind my vehicles for them to reverse out of a dangerous situation. You would think this would have been in the game by now considering it totes itself as being ultra realistic. In skirmish, you start the mission off with either no or a handful of infantry support units depending on which doctrine you pick before you start the game, which can be infuriating especially when you're trying to assault numerically superior entrenched infantry on a hill supported by mortars, machine guns, and tanks while you have some guys with rifles and a truck with a machine gun strapped to the back and little to no infantry or anti-tank support to speak of, which AGAIN, isn't realistic at all. And once again, this wouldn't be so bad if it weren't so difficult to utilize some of the features of the game like smoke grenades or even something as simple as making your units engage the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy. It was also a weird decision to make most of the heavy weapons in the game have the same ranges. For some reason, mortars have to be in range of AT weapons to bombard the position, light AT guns have only a slightly lower range than the heavier ones, heavy artillery has surprisingly short range, etc. At least in the OG Men of War it would scale even if the ranges were ridiculously short. The devs also didn't even bother to make the units in skirmish remotely accurate to the period that any of the missions take place in. Also, why did they decide to remove the swastika from Finnish vehicles? I understand Germany to an extent (not really, considering it's supposed to be a realistic game) but the hakaristi was completely separate from the Nazis and was first used in 1918 after a plane was given to them by Sweden, the leader of which used the swastika as a personal symbol. If you don't want to show that ♥♥♥♥, then don't make a game about world war 2, it's that simple.

Again, the design choices are odd and there are more that i'm just not remembering right now, but DESPITE ALL OF THAT, I could forgive it. Most of this stuff can be fixed with mods which is really what made the Men of War series so great. But I can't forgive the devs for REPEATEDLY releasing an unfinished product. I bought Ostfront in December of 2021 so most of the campaign missions had been fixed but I know that some of them were unplayable when the game was released and clearly no one had play tested them. And now, with the Talvisota DLC there is more unpolished slop. Spelling errors, bugs, unplayable areas, even on the Bagration map the assets for bridge on the right aren't even put together properly. I couldn't even finish the last mission in the Talvisota DLC because for some reason the Germans stopped spawning after the second wave. It also seems like they forgot to put the Finnish skirmish mission in and it took them an extra day to put it into the game. They charge people 18 dollars for a DLC that isn't even finished. Not to mention several people have noted that the devs are extremely rude if you critique their product, even if it's for things that really shouldn't even be broken in the first place. I think it's ridiculous that we are expected to sit here and put up with the lack of effort by dev teams to release a polished and playable game. If you're going to make somebody get a completely unrelated game just to play it, then release an overpriced DLC that adds a lackluster faction with reskinned units at least make it finished.

In conclusion, if you're a long time fan of Men of War, are willing to spend the money on both Call to Arms and Ostfront, and can deal with dumb AI or you are just going to have fun in the editor like I normally do, then yes the game is fun. But the single player missions, the skirmish, conquest, and the multiplayer all have some serious problems and at this stage the devs should really be focusing on the core game issues like AI and quality of life and not releasing an extortionately priced unpolished DLC.

117156536.review:
Amazing real time tactics game, focusing on immersive and realistic mechanics, with full control down to the inventory of the individual soldier. Much, MUCH better than the base game Call to Arms, only inheriting the base game engine from it. Takes to itself to be the spiritual successor to Men of War:Assault Squad 2, and I'd say it mostly succeeds. Plenty of mods to enhance and expand the experience, just like it's heritage of CtA and MOWAS2.

Very deep historically accurate roster of units, with split time periods of WW2 in Early, Mid and Late War inventories for the factions in game. Currenly it features only the Eastern Front, with Germany, USSR and now Finland with the Talvisota add-on DLC. Everything from basic infantry with even outdated WW1 weapons all the way into the largest tanks and artillery cannons. Manual control of everything is a big feature, you can and you should take control of your tanks to accurately shoot weakspots in enemy armor. If you ever played something like War Thunder or World of Tanks in the past, you should already be familiar with this concept, of what caliber gun can penetrate what kind of tank. Infantry combat is also deep, with whole squads bringing in all different roles, such as machinegunner, machinegunner assistant (with extra ammo), Squad leader, snipers, engineers, AT infantry, or even flamethrowers. They are all individually useful for their roles. The German Pionier squad will become one of your best friends. Good positioning of stationary weapons such as infantry support guns, mortars, AT guns, AA guns, all are extremely important.

Only weak spots of this game stem from having to utilize the CtA engine as it's base. It is a good evolution from the old GEM engine of MOWAS2, with greatly improved visuals, view range and framerate, but it also has... Not very good unit AI and pathing. And by not very good I mean *really* bad. You'll get used to manually splitting your infantry and controlling them yourself to try and minimize the babysitting you have to do with them to keep them alive. It's better than CtA, where they're literally braindead, but it's still not as good and responsive as old MOWAS2.

117108645.review:
This game is, for the most part, a very solid experience and provides something that I haven't seen from any other studio: a legitimate WWII battalion-level RTT. It has an impressive amount of vehicles, troop types, gun emplacements, artillery pieces, etc, allowing you to use a huge variety of tactics against your enemies, whether they be player or AI. It's basically the closest thing you're going to get to a WWII Total War game. Given these factors and the fun that I've had with the game so far, I have to give it a thumbs up, but I should clarify that it is a reluctant thumbs up.
The game has a litany of annoying and/or un-intuitive design choices, as well as a ton of bugs that seriously detract from its overall quality. First of all, the tutorial is atrocious, as it is so obviously designed by a dev who just assumes that the player will be able to magically guess how to carry out every action with their soldiers. They never give you any indication of which keys correspond with which actions and every weapon and vehicle seems to have its own wildly different set of key bindings. Additionally, there are no hotkeys at all for most orders, meaning that you will have to dig through layers of menus every time you simply want to give an order to a single soldier. This leaves the controls for the game feeling cumbersome and uncomfortable which is a huge deal in an RTT game where you are managing dozens or hundreds of soldiers across a battlefield that is rapidly evolving in real time.
Second, the AI is underwhelming and the game tries to compensate for that in a few less than adequate ways. AI units seem to have a hidden accuracy stat that makes them hit their target perfectly on the first shot every single time. I can't empirically prove it but my units just seem to have clearly worse accuracy. This means that if even a tiny sliver of one of your panzers is spotted by an enemy AT emplacement halfway across the map, you're getting hit and you're probably gonna lose a driver or gunner, rendering the thing practically useless. Of course, when MY units are firing at an enemy tank things all of a sudden seem to be very different. This, in addition to the fact that the AI can clearly see through the fog of war (a mechanic that only allows you to see enemies within the direct sight lines of your own troops), and WILL use that to its advantage to screw you over. I understand that the AI needs to have some crutches in order to make it more engaging to fight against but the devs have clearly chosen to take the easy route and just give it cheats instead of actually designing it to be truly intelligent.
Finally, the game suffers from a number of bugs that definitely should have been fixed by now. The cover system, one of the most fundamental features of how you manage your infantry, simply does not work. The option to place your men behind cover objects often just doesn't appear or it flickers, making it very difficult to get them exactly where you want. Sometimes they will go behind cover but then stand up straight even though they are under heavy fire. Again, its another thing that adds to the cumbersome nature of the game's controls, forcing you to think about things that you shouldn't have to, and making it harder to coordinate large battles with lots of units. On top of this, the pathfinding is completely broken and trucks/tanks will frequently move to a point, stop to re-adjust their facing, move to the next point, stop again, and so on. This means that it is nearly impossible to pull off a true Bewegungskrieg tactic which WWII is famed for, as tanks are terribly slow unless you are directly controlling them.
Ultimately, while these issues are bad, they do not outweigh the good that this game has to offer or the uniqueness of its gameplay. I just wish that the devs would not market this as a full release title and produce $20 DLC for it when it clearly should still be in early access until it has been more refined. Definitely only get this on sale, as the base $45 dollar asking price is absurd given the major problems the game still faces.
